w-id-012.title: Ayam Betutu Bali

instructions.1: Prepare the spice paste: Blend shallots, candlenuts, sambal oelek, Thai chilies, garlic, ginger, kencur root, turmeric, galangal, coriander, terasi, kaffir lime leaves, coconut oil, lemongrass, white pepper, salt, coconut sugar, and lime juice in a food processor until smooth.
instructions.2: Precook the vegetables: Sauté the shallots in coconut oil until golden, then add the spice paste and cook for 5 minutes.
instructions.3: Stuff the chicken with vegetables: Place the cassava leaves and cooked vegetables inside the chicken cavity.
instructions.4: Wrap the chicken and marinate: Wrap the chicken in banana leaves and then in aluminum foil, and let it marinate for 30 minutes.
instructions.5: If using an Instant Pot: Place the chicken in the pot and add 2 cups of water. Set the high pressure for 40 minutes.
instructions.6: If roasting: Place the chicken in a preheated oven at 180°C and roast for 1 hour and 30 minutes.
instructions.7: Serve the chicken with sambal matah if desired.

w-id-012.culturalNotes: Ayam Betutu Bali is a traditional dish from Bali, Indonesia, known for its spicy and aromatic flavors.

w-id-013.title: Vegetable Biryani

w-id-013-i12.name: carrots
w-id-013-i12.standardAmount: 6 carrots (peeled and cut in large chunks)

instructions.1: Wash the basmati rice under cool water until the liquid is no longer cloudy. Soak the rice in a bowl of clean, cool water for 30 minutes.
instructions.2: While the rice is soaking, put 6 cups of water in a pot along with the whole spices and salt. Cover and gently bring to a simmer.
instructions.3: After 30 minutes, bring the simmering pot of water to a full boil. Drain the soaked rice and add it to the pot. Gently boil for 5 minutes. Strain the rice and spread it in a large platter to stop the cooking.
instructions.4: In a large heavy-bottomed pot, heat the ghee and fry the sliced onion until deep brown. Remove the fried onion with a slotted spoon onto a plate lined with a paper towel and set aside.
instructions.5: Fry the potatoes, cauliflower, and carrots in the remaining ghee until browned on all sides. Remove and set aside.
instructions.6: In the same pot, fry the minced onion and tomato until soft. Add the garlic, ginger, sliced green chili peppers, and the spices. Stir until well combined and fragrant. Cool slightly, then stir in the yogurt. Add the chopped vegetables and stir to coat in the masala.
instructions.7: Scatter the raisins on top of the vegetables, then spoon on the parcooked rice. Smooth the surface and drizzle with rose water. Drizzle on the melted ghee if you want a more indulgent biryani. Cover and cook over low/medium-low for about 45 minutes until the rice is cooked through.
instructions.8: Taste the rice to make sure it is cooked to your liking. Tip onto a large family-style platter, stirring gently to combine all ingredients as you go. Top with reserved fried onion, slivered almonds, and cilantro.

w-id-013.culturalNotes: Biryani is a popular dish in Indonesia, often served on special occasions and family gatherings. It is known for its rich blend of spices and fresh vegetables.

w-id-014.title: Steamed Cake (Bolu Kukus Mekar)

instructions.1: Cut the gula Melaka into smaller pieces. Place it in a saucepan with coconut milk over low heat and stir until the sugar dissolves. Let the mixture cool completely before using.
instructions.2: Mix the dry ingredients (flour, salt, baking powder) in a bowl and set aside.
instructions.3: Fill your steamer with water and start boiling the water. Make sure there is enough water to steam the cake for at least 15 minutes on high heat. Wrap the lid with a cloth to prevent water condensation from dripping onto the cake. Line the muffin cups with paper liners.
instructions.4: Prepare the cake batter: Beat the egg with granulated sugar until the mixture becomes creamy. Add the oil and mix well. Add the liquid mixture (gula Melaka and coconut milk) and mix well. Add the dry ingredients and mix until the batter is smooth.
instructions.5: Pour the batter into the lined muffin cups. Place the cups in the steamer and steam for 15 minutes on high heat.
instructions.6: Let the cake cool slightly before serving.

w-id-014.culturalNotes: Steamed cake (Bolu Kukus Mekar) is a traditional Indonesian dessert, often served on special occasions and holidays.

w-id-015.title: Bubur Cha Cha

w-id-015-i8.name: sugar
w-id-015-i8.standardAmount: 120 gr (about 1/2 cup + 5 tsp, or more or less to taste)

instructions.1: Wash, peel, and cut the sweet potatoes and taro into small pieces.
instructions.2: Place the sweet potatoes and taro in a steamer and steam for 15 minutes until tender.
instructions.3: In a separate pot, place the tapioca pearls in boiling water and boil for 10 minutes until they become translucent and chewy.
instructions.4: In a large pot, combine coconut milk, water, sugar, salt, and pandan leaves, and bring to a boil over medium heat.
instructions.5: Add the steamed sweet potatoes and taro, and the cooked tapioca pearls to the coconut milk mixture, and stir well.
instructions.6: Let the mixture boil for another 5 minutes, then turn off the heat.
instructions.7: Serve Bubur Cha Cha hot or cold, as desired.

w-id-015.culturalNotes: Bubur Cha Cha is a traditional Nyonya dessert, a mix of sweet potatoes, taro, and tapioca pearls in coconut milk.

w-id-016.title: Bubur Ketan Hitam (Black Sticky Rice Dessert)

w-id-016-i3.name: Water
w-id-016-i3.standardAmount: 800 ml (1000 ml if cooking on the stove)

instructions.1: Soak the black glutinous rice for 30 minutes if cooking on the stove.
instructions.2: Break the rice in a blender or food processor if desired.
instructions.3: Add the rice, water, coconut sugar, and pandan leaves to the pressure cooker.
instructions.4: Close the pressure cooker and cook on high pressure for 20 minutes.
instructions.5: After cooking, let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes.
instructions.6: Add the coconut cream and salt, and mix well.
instructions.7: Serve the dessert hot or cold as desired.

w-id-016.culturalNotes: Bubur Ketan Hitam is a traditional Indonesian dessert often served on special occasions.

w-id-017.title: Cilok Bandung (Tapioca Balls with Peanut Sauce)

instructions.1: Prepare the peanut sauce: Blend the roasted peanuts, garlic, chilies, water, tamarind paste, palm sugar, Kecap manis, and salt in a blender until smooth. Cook the sauce over medium heat for 5 minutes until it thickens.
instructions.2: Prepare the tapioca dough: Mix tapioca starch, all-purpose flour, scallions, chicken powder, salt, sugar, and white pepper in a bowl. Gradually add the hot boiling water and knead until the dough is smooth and pliable.
instructions.3: Shape the dough into balls: Cut the dough into small pieces and shape them into small balls.
instructions.4: Boil the tapioca dough: Bring water to a boil in a pot and add the balls. Boil for 5 minutes until they float to the surface.
instructions.5: Serve: Pour the peanut sauce over the boiled balls and serve hot with your favorite chili sauce.

w-id-017.culturalNotes: Cilok is a popular dish in Indonesia, especially in Bandung. It is served as an appetizer or a light meal.

w-id-018.title: Pandan Kaya Swiss Roll (Bolu Gulung Kaya)

instructions.1: Spray a 9 x 13 x 1 inch baking pan with non-stick cooking spray or brush with oil, then line the bottom and sides with parchment paper.
instructions.2: Prepare the cake batter: Mix the egg yolks with the cooking oil and coconut milk until well combined. Add the flour and salt, and mix until the batter is smooth.
instructions.3: Prepare the meringue: Beat the egg whites with the sugar and cream of tartar (or lemon juice or vinegar) until stiff peaks form.
instructions.4: Fold the meringue into the cake batter gently until well combined.
instructions.5: Pour the batter into the prepared pan and spread evenly.
instructions.6: Bake in a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F) for 15-20 minutes or until golden brown.
instructions.7: Let the cake cool slightly, then trim the four edges.
instructions.8: Make 4 shallow slits on the surface of the cake.
instructions.9: Spread the kaya jam over the surface of the cake.
instructions.10: Roll up the cake gently using the parchment paper to maintain its shape.
instructions.11: Remove the parchment paper immediately after rolling.
instructions.12: Serve the roll warm or cold as desired.

w-id-018.culturalNotes: Srikaya is a type of jam made from coconut milk and eggs, and it is popular in Indonesian and Malay cuisine.

w-id-019.title: Indonesian Chicken Curry (Kari Ayam)

instructions.1: Wash the chicken parts.
instructions.2: In a food processor or mortar and pestle, grind the garlic, ginger, candlenuts, turmeric, galangal, hot chilies (if using), and terasi into a paste (bumbu).
instructions.3: In a wok or skillet, cook the paste over medium heat for 1 minute.
instructions.4: Add the chicken parts to the wok, and brown them.
instructions.5: Add the shallots, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, and salam leaves to the wok, and sauté for another minute.
instructions.6: Add the coconut milk and bring to a light boil.
instructions.7: Simmer on low heat for 10 minutes.

w-id-019.culturalNotes: Indonesian curry is a popular dish in Indonesia, known for its rich and complex flavors.

w-id-020.title: Dadar Gulung (Caramelized Coconut Pancakes)

instructions.1: Combine all the pancake ingredients in a large mixing bowl.
instructions.2: Whisk the ingredients well.
instructions.3: Strain the mixture if necessary to remove any lumps.
instructions.4: Heat a non-stick pan and brush with extra butter.
instructions.5: Ladle the pancake mixture into the pan until the bottom is thinly covered.
instructions.6: Flip the pancake when it is ready.
instructions.7: Repeat until the mixture is finished.
instructions.8: Place the water and sugar in a saucepan and heat until the sugar is dissolved.
instructions.9: Add the remaining filling ingredients and cook until all the liquid has evaporated.
instructions.10: Remove the mixture from the heat and discard the cooked pandan leaf.
instructions.11: Place equal portions of the filling in each pancake.
instructions.12: Roll the crepe into a parcel and garnish with fresh pandan leaves.

w-id-020.culturalNotes: Dadar Gulung is a traditional Indonesian dish often served as a breakfast or light dessert.

w-id-021.title: Stewed Pounded Cassava Leaves in Coconut Milk (Daun Ubi Tumbuk)

instructions.1: Wash the cassava leaves and cut them into small pieces.
instructions.2: Wash the pea eggplant and cut them in half.
instructions.3: If using dried shrimp instead of anchovies, wash them and soak in warm water until soft, then finely chop and set aside.
instructions.4: In a bowl, mix the shallots, garlic, red chilies, ginger, and turmeric, then grind until smooth.
instructions.5: Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat, then add the ground spices and stir for 2-3 minutes until golden brown.
instructions.6: Add the kaffir lime leaves, torch ginger buds, and lemongrass, and stir for a minute.
instructions.7: Add the water and bring to a boil, then add the cassava leaves, pea eggplant, and anchovies (or dried shrimp), and stir.
instructions.8: Add the thick coconut milk, sugar, and salt (and chicken powder if desired), and bring to a boil over low heat for 20-25 minutes until the leaves are tender.
instructions.9: Serve the dish hot.

w-id-021.culturalNotes: Daun ubi tumbuk is a traditional Indonesian dish usually served as part of a lunch or dinner meal.

w-id-022.title: Dendeng Balado

instructions.1: Place all the ingredients for the spice paste in a food processor and process into a paste. Add a bit of water if needed.
instructions.2: Rub the beef with the marinade and let it marinate for 30 minutes.
instructions.3: Place the beef in a medium-sized pot. Add water just until it barely covers the beef and let it cook for about 45 minutes to 1 hour or until the beef is tender but not falling apart.
instructions.4: Remove the beef from the pot and let it cool down a little. Thinly slice the beef across the grain. Use a heavy object (such as a pestle) to pound the meat to about 1/4-inch thick.
instructions.5: Preheat a small to medium non-stick pan with about 1 Tbsp of oil. Pan fry the beef slices until they are lightly brown and dry.
instructions.6: Serve the dendeng with sambal.

w-id-022.culturalNotes: Dendeng Balado is a traditional Indonesian dish often served with rice and sambal.

w-id-023.title: Crab and Shrimp Egg Foo Young

instructions.1: Cook the proteins separately: In a pan, heat 1 tsp of sesame oil and sauté the minced garlic for 1 minute. Add the shredded carrot and sauté for 1 minute. Add the crab meat and chopped shrimp and sauté for 2-3 minutes until they turn white. Set aside.
instructions.2: Prepare the egg mixture: In a bowl, beat the eggs with 1 tsp of sesame oil, sugar, soy sauce, and ground white pepper. Add the cooked proteins and shredded carrot and mix well.
instructions.3: Cook the egg foo young: In a large pan, heat 1/3 cup of cooking oil over medium heat. Add the egg mixture and gently stir until golden brown. Cook in batches if necessary.
instructions.4: Make the gravy: In a small bowl, mix chicken stock, sesame oil, oyster sauce, soy sauce, sugar, and cornstarch. Pour the mixture into a pan over medium heat and stir until thickened.
instructions.5: Serve the egg foo young with the gravy and garnish with the green parts of the green onion.

w-id-023.culturalNotes: Egg Foo Young is a popular Chinese dish in Indonesia, often served as part of the Chinese-Indonesian cuisine.

w-id-024.title: Empanada Dough

instructions.1: In a medium bowl, whisk sugar and salt into the flour.
instructions.2: Using a pastry cutter (or two knives), cut the butter into the flour until it is pea-sized.
instructions.3: Add in water – a little at a time until a shaggy mass forms.
instructions.4: Press together with your hands. It will be a little dry to the touch. Shape into 2 flatted disks, wrap in saran and refrigerate while working on your filling.
instructions.5: After at least 30 minutes, remove dough from fridge and roll thinly, on a slightly floured work-surface.
instructions.6: Cut out shapes and fill (use a round cutter – either 3 1/2 or 5″ in diameter). Roll the edges to seal…
instructions.7: Now you can make beef empanadas or apple empanadas or… whatever your heart desires!

w-id-024.culturalNotes: Empanada is a popular dish in Indonesia, consisting of pastries filled with meat, vegetables, or fruits.

w-ir-001.title: Abgoosht (Persian Meat and Potato Soup)

instructions.1: Rinse the beans and drain them. Transfer the beans into the Instant Pot and add 2 teaspoons of kosher salt and enough water to cover the beans by 1 inch, about 6 cups of water.
instructions.2: Close the lid and seal. Set the Instant Pot to manual (or pressure cook on newer models) set to high pressure for 5 minutes. Allow for 20 minutes natural pressure release.
instructions.3: When done, drain the beans and discard the water. Reserve the beans.
instructions.4: Heat the Instant Pot to sauté on high and add 1 tablespoon of extra virgin olive oil.
instructions.5: Season the meat with 1 teaspoon of kosher salt and 1/2 teaspoon of black pepper. Brown the shanks on both sides in batches, 3-5 minutes for each side. Once browned, transfer the shanks to a plate and reserve.
instructions.6: Add 1 tablespoon of oil to the hot pot then add chopped onions. Cook until softened then season with 1/2 teaspoon of kosher salt and 1/2 teaspoon of turmeric. Cook for 5 more minutes.
instructions.7: Start adding the shanks, chopped potatoes, and beans back into the pot with the onions.
instructions.8: Pierce the dried limes all over with a sharp knife and press them into the pot.
instructions.9: Whisk together tomato paste with beef broth then pour into the pot.
instructions.10: Close the lid and seal. Set the Instant Pot to manual (or pressure cook on newer models) set to high pressure for 35 minutes. Allow for 20 minutes natural pressure release.
instructions.11: Transfer the meat and bones to a large mixing bowl. When it cools, discard the bones and extra fat, leaving just the meat in the bowl. Shred with a fork.
instructions.12: Strain out the remaining solids from the broth. Reserve the broth. This is the cherished soup, abgoosht.
instructions.13: Some people serve the soup with the solids, but most mash the solids to make goosht koobideh.
instructions.14: Transfer all of the strained solids to the mixing bowl with the meat. Use a potato masher or food mallet to smash and press the solids into a paste. Add broth as needed, to smooth out the paste. It should have the consistency of Mexican refried beans. Adjust the seasoning to taste by adding more salt or more limoo omami (the powdered kind).
instructions.15: To serve the broth, fill a bowl with bite-size pieces of sangak or lavash then pour the broth in.
instructions.16: Serve the goosht koobideh with more bread, torshi (Persian pickled vegetables), radishes, and fresh herbs (sabzi khordan).

w-ir-001.culturalNotes: Abgoosht is a traditional Iranian dish often served at family gatherings and social occasions. It is typically served with bread, pickled vegetables, and herbs.

w-ir-002.title: Advieh (Persian Spice Mix)

instructions.1: Add all the spices to a bowl.
instructions.2: Stir the spices well to ensure they are evenly mixed.
instructions.3: Transfer the mixture to a tightly sealed jar.
instructions.4: Shake the jar well to ensure the spices are fully mixed.
instructions.5: Store the mixture in the spice cabinet and use it for rice dishes, stews, and kebabs.

w-ir-002.culturalNotes: Advieh is a traditional Persian spice mix used to enhance the flavor of dishes.

w-ir-003.title: Albaloo Polo (Sour Cherry Rice)

instructions.1: Soak the rice in a medium-sized bowl with water. Gently wash the rice by stirring it in the water with your hand. Pour out the water and repeat two more times. After washing the rice a third time, rinse and then cover with water and soak.
instructions.2: In a small bowl, combine the ground saffron with 1 tablespoon of hot water and set aside.
instructions.3: If using fresh sour cherries, clean and pit them. If using frozen cherries, thaw first.
instructions.4: Place the cherries and sugar in a saucepan and cook on medium-low heat for 15 minutes. Strain out the cherries.
instructions.5: Continue cooking until the juices are syrupy. Return the cherries to the syrup and remove from heat and reserve.
instructions.6: In a large non-stick pot, add 6 cups of water and 1 tablespoon of salt and bring to a boil. When the water has come to a boil, pour out the water in the bowl containing the soaking rice. Add the strained rice to the boiling water.
instructions.7: When the water comes to a boil again and the rice floats to the top of the pot (approximately 6 minutes), pour the contents of the pot into a fine colander.
instructions.8: Return the pot to the stove over medium heat. Add 2 tablespoons of butter and 1 teaspoon of saffron. When the butter has melted, add enough rice to cover the bottom of the pot. Mix with the saffron butter and gently spread flat in the bottom of the pot.
instructions.9: Scatter about 1/3 of the rice over this buttered layer. Spoon 1/3 of the sour cherries over the rice, using some of the syrup but not a lot. Repeat layering in rice and sour cherries until all the cherries and rice are in the pot.
instructions.10: Reserve the leftover syrup.
instructions.11: Using the handle of a long wooden spoon, poke a hole down to the bottom of the pot. This allows the steam to escape.
instructions.12: Cover the lid of your pot with a clean towel or several paper towels, and set firmly over your pot to prevent steam from escaping. Reduce heat to low and continue cooking the rice for 45 minutes.
instructions.13: While the rice is cooking, prepare the meatballs. Mix the ingredients (except for the oil) together in a large mixing bowl. Scoop out enough meat to form a 1-inch meatball, approximately 20.
instructions.14: Once all meatballs have been formed, heat a large pan over medium-high heat and add oil. When the oil is hot, begin frying the meatballs until browned all over. This will take about 10-15 minutes.
instructions.15: Transfer the meatballs to a large bowl. Mix in 1-2 tablespoons of the reserved cherry syrup and coat the meatballs evenly.
instructions.16: When the rice is done cooking, scoop out about 1/2 cup of cooked rice and transfer to a bowl. Stir in the saffron water and mix until golden.
instructions.17: Scoop out the rest of the rice onto a serving platter and top with the saffron rice.
instructions.18: Break up the tahdig (crust) and place around the rice. Arrange the meatballs on the serving platter. Garnish with almonds and pistachios and serve.

w-ir-003.culturalNotes: Albaloo Polo is a traditional Iranian dish served on special occasions. It is known for its sweet and sour flavor from the cherries and saffron.

w-ir-004.title: Persian Barbari Bread

instructions.1: Place the flour, salt, sugar, oil, and yeast in the bowl of a stand mixer with a dough hook.
instructions.2: Turn the stand mixer on and set it on slow speed. Add the water slowly while the mixer is running.
instructions.3: Once the dough comes together, turn the speed to medium and knead for 10 minutes.
instructions.4: Cover the bowl with a kitchen towel and let it sit for 30 minutes.
instructions.5: Place the dough on a floured surface and divide it into two. Shape into balls and cover with a kitchen towel. Let the dough rise for 30 minutes.
instructions.6: Meanwhile, mix the glaze ingredients in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a simmer and stir until it thickens. This will take about 3-4 minutes. Set aside to cool.
instructions.7: After 30 minutes, place one of the balls on parchment paper. Flatten the dough using your hand into an oval shape. Using your fingers (except the thumbs) make indentations on the bread. Brush with the glaze and top with sesame seeds. Transfer the parchment paper to a baking sheet, cover with plastic wrap, and let it sit for another 20-30 minutes.
instructions.8: Preheat the oven to 225°C (440°F). Once the oven is hot, uncover the baking sheet and place the bread in the oven. Bake for 18 minutes until golden and cooked. Let it sit for 10 minutes before you slice it.

w-ir-004.culturalNotes: Barbari bread is a traditional Iranian bread known for its crispy exterior and soft interior. It is typically served with main dishes.

w-ir-005.title: Persian Yogurt Spinach Dip (Borani Esfenaj)

instructions.1: Heat a large frying pan over medium-high heat and add olive oil.
instructions.2: Add onion and sauté until they start to soften.
instructions.3: Reduce heat to medium-low and cook until onions are slightly browned, about 7 minutes.
instructions.4: Add spinach and garlic and cook for 5 minutes, or until spinach is wilted and cooked. Remove from heat and let cool.
instructions.5: In a large bowl, add cooled spinach mixture with yogurt, salt, and pepper. Mix until combined, cover, and refrigerate for 2 hours prior to serving.
instructions.6: When ready to serve, transfer to a serving bowl and garnish with walnuts.

w-ir-005.culturalNotes: Borani is a popular dish in Iran, served as an appetizer or side salad.

w-ir-006.title: Air Fryer Turkey Cutlets (Persian Kotlet)

w-ir-006-i12.name: olive oil or non-stick cooking spray

instructions.1: In a medium-sized pot, add the potatoes and cover with water. Bring to a boil and cook until the potatoes are fork-tender, about 10-15 minutes.
instructions.2: Drain the water and mash the potatoes thoroughly. Transfer to a large mixing bowl and allow to cool to room temperature, about 10-15 minutes.
instructions.3: Grate the onion by hand or using a food processor. Squeeze out the excess juice and place the grated onion with the mashed potatoes.
instructions.4: In the same mixing bowl, add the ground turkey, baking soda, flour, egg, and seasonings. Mix by hand until fully incorporated.
instructions.5: Chill the mixture in the refrigerator for a couple of hours to make it easier to form into patties and allow the flavors to meld together. This step is optional.
instructions.6: Pour the breadcrumbs on a plate. Take a 2-inch ball of the meat mixture and flatten it into an oval shape about the size of your hand and up to ½-inch thick.
instructions.7: Press both sides of the cutlets into the breadcrumbs and reserve them on a large platter or baking sheet.
instructions.8: Generously spray both sides of the prepared cutlets with olive oil or non-stick cooking spray.
instructions.9: Set your air fryer to 'air fry' and set the time for 14 minutes. Once preheated, add the cutlets in a single layer. My fryer fits 5-6 pieces.
instructions.10: At the halfway mark, use a spatula to flip the cutlets over and continue air frying until done.
instructions.11: Repeat until all the cutlets are air fried.

w-ir-006.culturalNotes: Kotlet is a popular dish in Iran, often served as part of a lunch or dinner meal.

w-ir-007.title: Fesenjān

instructions.1: Purée the onion until smooth in a food processor.
instructions.2: Add the walnuts to the onion and purée until a thick paste is formed.
instructions.3: Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
instructions.4: In a large skillet over medium-high heat, add the olive oil. When the oil is hot, add the chicken and cook until browned, about 3-5 minutes.
instructions.5: Turn the chicken thighs over and brown the other side. Transfer the chicken to a serving dish and reserve.
instructions.6: Transfer the walnut-onion mixture to the hot pan and spread it evenly on the bottom of the skillet.
instructions.7: Heat the mixture over medium-low. When it starts to brown, stir and remix the paste and spread it evenly again.
instructions.8: Reduce heat to low and repeat every 10-15 minutes. Cook until the walnut-onion mixture is deep brown in color and crumbly, about 1 hour.
instructions.9: Stir in the saffron and pomegranate molasses.
instructions.10: Cut the chicken thighs into strips and add to the pomegranate mixture. Cover and simmer until the color darkens, about 20 minutes.
instructions.11: If the sauce needs thinning, drizzle in water as needed.
instructions.12: Transfer the stew to a serving dish and garnish with pomegranate arils.

w-ir-007.culturalNotes: Fesenjān is a traditional Iranian dish often served on special occasions.

w-ir-008.title: Khoresh Gheymeh with Yellow Split Peas

instructions.1: Peel and finely chop the onion.
instructions.2: In a large bowl, mix together the beef, 1 tsp of salt, 1/2 tsp of black pepper, 1/2 tsp of turmeric, and flour until the meat is evenly coated. Set aside.
instructions.3: Press the “Sauté” function key on your Instant Pot. Select “More” temperature with the “Adjust” key. When the Instant Pot displays “Hot,” add the olive oil.
instructions.4: When the oil is hot, add the chopped onions and sauté until they start to brown.
instructions.5: Season the onions with 1/2 tsp of salt and 1/2 tsp of turmeric and cook for another 2-3 minutes.
instructions.6: Stir in the reserved stew meat and brown the meat all over.
instructions.7: When the meat is browned, add the beef broth. Using a wooden spoon, scrape the bottom of the pot to remove browned bits.
instructions.8: Stir in the tomato paste until combined. Add the diced tomatoes.
instructions.9: Carefully pierce the dried limes with a sharp knife several times. If you prefer a more sour, lemony stew, add up to 5 dried limes. If you’re unsure, start with three. You can add lemon juice later to adjust the flavor to your preference.
instructions.10: Place the lid on your Instant Pot, turn the vent to “Seal,” and set the Instant Pot to “Meat/Stew” for 20 minutes.
instructions.11: Once the timer goes off and the stew is cooked, let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes, then release the remaining pressure manually. You can also let all the pressure release naturally if you have time.
instructions.12: Using a spoon, press the dried limes flat to remove air and let them sink into the stew.
instructions.13: Stir in the cinnamon. Rinse the yellow split peas and drain. Add the split peas to the stew.
instructions.14: Close the lid of the Instant Pot, turn the vent to “Seal,” and set the Instant Pot to “Manual” (or “Pressure Cook” on newer models) on high pressure for 15 minutes. Release the pressure manually very carefully. If the stew is thick, stir in 1 cup of water.
instructions.15: Transfer the stew to a serving dish and top with shoestring potatoes.
instructions.16: You can also peel and chop 1 large russet potato. Once fried crisp, you can use these potatoes to top your stew.
instructions.17: Serve the stew with steamed basmati rice.

w-ir-008.culturalNotes: Khoresh Gheymeh is a traditional Iranian dish typically served with steamed basmati rice. It is known for its rich and tangy flavor from dried limes and yellow split peas.

w-ir-009.title: Ghormeh Sabzi

instructions.1: Soak the red beans in water for 1 hour.
instructions.2: Remove unnecessary fat from the meat and cut it into smaller pieces.
instructions.3: Heat the oil in a large pot and fry the onions at high temperature for 1-2 minutes.
instructions.4: Add the meat and cook for another 1-2 minutes.
instructions.5: Reduce the heat to the lowest level. The meat will release a significant amount of juice which will contribute to the flavor of the stew.
instructions.6: Stir in the parsley, spinach, coriander leaves, and fried ghormeh sabzi herbs.
instructions.7: Stir in boiling water (about 0.5 L or until the consistency is right).
instructions.8: Stir in the cooked, drained beans. Simmer for about 2-3 hours over low heat. The longer the better.
instructions.9: Soak the dried limes in hot water for 15 minutes and puncture each of them with a fork.
instructions.10: Add the dried limes, turmeric, pepper, and salt to the stew. Simmer for another 30-60 minutes.
instructions.11: If desired, let the stew cool down and store it in a fridge. The taste is better over the next two days.
instructions.13: Grind the saffron and sugar together in a mortar. Add about 1 tablespoon boiling water. Toss some of the cooked rice with the saffron water to color it.
instructions.14: Serve the stew hot in its own bowl. Serve the plain rice in a separate bowl, topped with the saffron rice.

w-ir-009.culturalNotes: Ghormeh Sabzi is a traditional main dish in Iran, known for its rich flavors and the distinctive taste of dried limes.

w-ir-010.title: Kabab Torsh

instructions.1: Cut the ribeye into 1-inch chunks and place them in a bowl.
instructions.2: Place the pomegranate molasses, walnuts, olive oil, garlic, mint, parsley, and white onion in the bowl of a food processor. Blend until all is combined and a paste is formed. Add more olive oil if the texture isn't right yet.
instructions.3: Toss the beef with the paste and make sure all the pieces are well coated. Cover the bowl with a plastic wrap and refrigerate overnight.
instructions.4: When you're ready to grill, take the bowl out of the refrigerator and let the beef come to room temperature. Preheat the grill to medium high.
instructions.5: Sprinkle the saffron over 2 cubes of ice and let it melt completely. This will be your bloomed saffron. Melt the butter and then mix it with the bloomed saffron. Set aside.
instructions.6: Thread the beef pieces on skewers and place them on the grill. Grill for 4 to 5 minutes on each side until the meat is done to your preference. Brush with the bloomed saffron and melted butter mixture, then season with salt.
instructions.7: Remove the kabobs from the skewers using a thin bread such as lavash or just a fork.

w-ir-010.culturalNotes: Kabab Torsh is a traditional Iranian dish known for its tangy and sweet flavors from pomegranate and walnuts.

w-ir-011.title: Air Fryer Kebab Koobideh

instructions.1: Peel and quarter the onions, then place them in a food processor with the metal blade and process until smooth.
instructions.2: Pour the onion purée through a strainer placed over a bowl and drain the juice. Reserve the onion juice.
instructions.3: Using the food processor again, add alternating layers of ground beef, strained onions, and salt. You may need to do this in batches.
instructions.4: Process until combined, pausing to scrape down the sides. The mixture will become fluffy and light in color. Transfer the mixture to a large mixing bowl.
instructions.5: Knead the mixture like bread dough, dipping your hands in the onion water to keep the meat from sticking. The more you knead, the lighter the kebab. The texture should be airy, not a solid mass.
instructions.6: Allow the mixture to marinate in the refrigerator for 2-4 hours.
instructions.7: Take a tennis ball-sized amount of the meat mixture and shape it into a flat sausage-shaped kebab and place it on a baking sheet.
instructions.8: Place the kebabs in one layer in the air fryer and cook at 375°F for 10 minutes, flipping them over at the halfway mark.
instructions.9: Ensure the internal temperature of the kebabs reaches 145°F using a meat thermometer.

w-ir-011.culturalNotes: Kebab Koobideh is a popular type of kebab in Iran, typically served with rice and vegetables.

w-ir-012.title: Khoresh Bademjan

instructions.1: Peel the eggplants, keeping the stem intact, and cut them in half lengthwise. Sprinkle both sides with 1 tbsp of salt and place them on paper towels over a cooling rack. Cover with more paper towels and place a heavy baking sheet on top for 1 hour to remove the bitter water.
instructions.2: In a large bowl, mix the beef stew meat, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp black pepper, 1/4 tsp turmeric, and flour.
instructions.3: Heat a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat and add 1 tbsp of olive oil. When the oil is hot, add the chopped onions.
instructions.4: Cook the onions until they start to soften, about 5-7 minutes, then add 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp black pepper, and 1/4 tsp turmeric.
instructions.5: Cook for 2 minutes, then add the stew meat and brown all sides, about 7 minutes.
instructions.6: Stir in the beef broth and use a wooden spoon to scrape up the browned bits of meat from the bottom of the pot.
instructions.7: Stir in the tomato paste, rinsed yellow split peas, and dried limes. Add the diced tomatoes, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 2 hours.
instructions.8: Add the cinnamon and sour grapes and cook for an additional 10-15 minutes.
instructions.9: After 1 hour, squeeze the eggplants dry with paper towels and remove the excess salt.
instructions.10: Heat a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat and add 2 tbsp of olive oil. Fry the eggplants in batches until both sides are browned. Drain the fried eggplants on paper towels to remove excess oil.
instructions.11: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
instructions.12: In a 13x9-inch Pyrex dish, pour the stew in. Layer the fried eggplants over it. Layer the sliced tomatoes over the eggplants (optional).
instructions.13: Cover with foil and bake in the oven for 30 minutes.

w-ir-012.culturalNotes: Khoresh Bademjan is a famous dish in Iranian cuisine, typically served with rice.

w-ir-013.title: Persian Celery Stew

instructions.1: In a large bowl, mix beef stew meat with 1/2 teaspoon salt, 1/4 teaspoon black pepper, 1/4 teaspoon turmeric, and 2 teaspoons flour until the meat is evenly coated.
instructions.2: Heat a large Dutch oven over medium heat and add 1 tablespoon of olive oil. When the oil is hot, add the chopped onions. Cook until the onions start to soften, about 7 minutes, then add 1/2 teaspoon salt, 1/4 teaspoon black pepper, and 1/2 teaspoon turmeric.
instructions.3: Cook for 2 minutes, then raise the heat to medium-high and add the stew meat. Brown the meat on all sides, about 7 minutes.
instructions.4: Stir in beef broth and lemon juice. Use a wooden spoon to scrape up the browned bits of meat from the bottom of the pot.
instructions.5: Add the dried limes to the stew, reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and simmer for 2 hours, stirring the stew every 30 minutes.
instructions.6: Using a food processor (or chop finely with a knife) chop the parsley, mint, and spinach.
instructions.7: Heat a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat and add 1 tablespoon of olive oil. Sauté the chopped greens for 5 minutes, then add them to the meat mixture.
instructions.8: Add another 1 tablespoon of olive oil to the hot skillet and sauté the chopped celery. Cook for 5 minutes, then add it to the stew along with the ground saffron.
instructions.9: Cook the stew covered over low heat for another 45 minutes.
instructions.10: If using rhubarb, stir it in during the last 20 minutes of cooking.

w-ir-013.culturalNotes: Khoresh karafs is a popular dish in Iran, typically served with white rice.

w-ir-014.title: Green Almond Stew (Khoresh Chaghaleh Badoom)

instructions.1: In a large bowl, mix beef stew meat with 1/2 teaspoon salt, 1/4 teaspoon black pepper, 1/4 teaspoon turmeric, and 2 teaspoons flour until the meat is evenly coated.
instructions.2: Heat a large Dutch oven over medium heat and add 1 tablespoon of olive oil.
instructions.3: When the oil is hot, add the chopped onions.
instructions.4: Cook until the onions start to soften, about 7 minutes, then add 1/2 teaspoon salt, 1/4 teaspoon black pepper, and 1/2 teaspoon turmeric.
instructions.5: Cook for 2 minutes, then raise the heat to medium-high and add the stew meat, browning all sides for about 7 minutes.
instructions.6: Stir in beef broth and lemon juice, and use a wooden spoon to scrape up the browned bits of meat from the bottom of the pot.
instructions.7: Add the dried limes, reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and simmer for 2 hours, stirring the stew every 30 minutes.
instructions.8: Using a food processor (or chop finely with a knife), chop the parsley, mint, and spinach.
instructions.9: Heat a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat and add 1 tablespoon of olive oil.
instructions.10: Sauté the chopped greens for 5 minutes, then add them to the meat mixture along with the ground saffron.
instructions.11: Cook the stew covered over low heat for another 30 minutes.
instructions.12: Cut the green almonds in half and remove the inner seed.
instructions.13: Stir in the halved green almonds into the stew, cover the pot, and cook for 30 minutes.

w-ir-014.culturalNotes: Green Almond Stew (Khoresh Chaghaleh Badoom) is a traditional Iranian dish known for its sweet and sour flavor. It is typically served with rice.

w-ir-015.title: Fried Kibbeh (Bulgur & Meat Parcels)

w-ir-015-i7.name: yogurt, hummus, salad and lemon wedges to serve

instructions.1: For the filling, heat the oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Cook the onion for 10 mins until softened. Stir in the mince and cook until well browned. Stir through the pine nuts (if using) and season well with salt, pepper, and a pinch of the spice mix. Remove from the heat and set aside to cool completely.
instructions.2: Meanwhile, tip the bulgur wheat into a bowl and cover with cold water. Set aside to soak for 20 mins. Drain well.
instructions.3: Add the drained bulgur to a food processor along with the 500g mince, chopped onion, 1 tsp salt, ½ tsp black pepper, and dried spices. Whizz until smooth, adding in a couple of tablespoons of water if the mixture feels a little dry.
instructions.4: Wet your hands and scoop out a small portion (roughly 65g) of the kibbeh mixture. Shape it into a ball (you should get 22 balls in total), then gently hollow out the centre with your finger to create a shell.
instructions.5: Spoon a little of the cooled filling into the centre, then carefully seal the opening. Shape into an oval with slightly pointed ends. Repeat with the remaining mixture.
instructions.6: Half-fill a heavy-bottomed pan with vegetable oil and heat to 180C or until a cube of bread browns within 30 seconds. Fry the kibbeh in batches for 4-5 mins, turning occasionally until crisp and golden. Remove using a slotted spoon and drain on kitchen paper. Serve with yogurt, hummus, salad, and lemon wedges for squeezing over.

w-ir-015.culturalNotes: Kibbeh is a popular dish in Arabic cuisine, especially in the Levant. It is usually served as a main dish with yogurt, hummus, and salads.

w-ir-016.title: Kofta

instructions.1: Mix the ground lamb with the finely chopped onion, garlic, cinnamon, cumin, black pepper, salt, parsley, cilantro, and bread crumbs.
instructions.2: Shape the meat mixture into small balls.
instructions.3: Heat the olive oil in a pan over medium heat, add the meatballs, and cook until golden brown on all sides.
instructions.4: Add a little water and let the kofta cook for 20 minutes until fully cooked.
instructions.5: Serve hot with rice or bread.

w-ir-016.culturalNotes: Kofta is a popular dish in Iran and is usually served with rice and bread.

w-ir-017.title: Kuku Sabzi (Persian Herb Quiche)

instructions.1: Using a mortar and pestle, grind the saffron threads until powdered (about 1/8 teaspoon).
instructions.2: Add the hot water and swish it around. Let saffron steep in the hot water and set aside.
instructions.3: Chop the green onions and transfer to a mixing bowl. Add chopped parsley, cilantro, and dill to the bowl.
instructions.4: Heat your instant pot to sauté. When pot is hot, add olive oil. Add chopped herbs and sauté for 1-2 minutes.
instructions.5: Stir in dried fenugreek and continue cooking until herbs are dark green and cooked through, about minutes.
instructions.6: Transfer herbs to a mixing bowl and let it cool to room temperature. Rinse out and clean inside of instant pot.
instructions.7: When herbs are cool, stir in walnuts, zereshk, salt, pepper, and baking powder.
instructions.8: Whisk together eggs and stir in with the herb mixture.
instructions.9: Lightly oil a 7 x 3-inch cake pan or bowl. This bowl needs to fit inside your instant pot. Pour herb mixture into prepared pan/bowl.
instructions.10: Pour 1 1/2 cups water into your instant pot. Put your pan/bowl in your instant pot's sling/rack and gently place inside the instant pot with the water.
instructions.11: Close and lock the lid, making sure the steam valve is set to seal. Cook on high pressure for 20 minutes with 10 minute natural release. Release any remaining steam and slowly unlock and remove the lid.
instructions.12: Using the sling handles, gently lift the pan out and let it cool for 5-10 minutes. Cut into wedges and serve warm or cold.

w-ir-017.culturalNotes: Kuku Sabzi is a traditional Iranian dish made from fresh herbs and eggs. It is usually served on special occasions and celebrations.

w-ir-018.title: Turkish Delight (Lokum)

instructions.1: Brush the bottom and sides of a 9x9 inch baking pan with a bit of oil. Then line it with parchment paper and set aside.
instructions.2: In a 4 quart saucepan, place the water, sugar, and cornstarch. Place the saucepan over medium high heat. Once it comes to a simmer, lower the heat to medium and stir constantly until it thickens and has the consistency of gel. The mixture will be thick but still pourable.
instructions.3: Add the red food coloring and stir to combine. If you like it darker, add more food coloring. Cook for another 10 minutes and then turn the heat off.
instructions.4: Pour the mixture into the prepared baking pan and let it sit at room temperature for 4 hours or until solid.
instructions.5: Mix the powdered sugar with some cornstarch and sprinkle half of it on a clean surface such as a cutting board. Gently flip the solid lokum onto the board and top it with more cornstarch and powdered sugar mixture. Using a large knife, slice the lokum vertically and horizontally into 1 inch cubes.
instructions.6: Toss the cubes in the cornstarch and powdered sugar mix again and plate.

w-ir-018.culturalNotes: Lokum is a traditional Turkish sweet and is a popular dessert in the Middle East.

w-ir-019.title: Persian Rosettes (nan panjareh)

instructions.1: Combine cornstarch, flour, and milk in a bowl using an electric mixer until a thick paste forms.
instructions.2: In a second bowl, whisk together eggs and rosewater.
instructions.3: Stir the egg mixture into the flour mixture until thoroughly combined.
instructions.4: Heat the oil in a heavy stainless-steel pot with high sides or a deep fryer to 193°C (380°F).
instructions.5: Submerge the rosette iron completely into the hot oil for 2 minutes until it is piping hot.
instructions.6: Dip the hot iron into the batter. Do not cover the top of the rosette mold with batter.
instructions.7: Quickly submerge the batter-covered rosette iron into the hot oil. Bubbles will form around the rosette.
instructions.8: After 5-10 seconds, gently shake the rosette off the iron and continue to fry until golden, flipping the cookie over to brown evenly. The rosette should be golden and finished frying in about 30 seconds.
instructions.9: Using a slotted spoon, chopsticks, or a small strainer, remove the rosette from the hot oil and place it on a tray lined with paper towels to remove excess oil.
instructions.10: Reheat the rosette iron in the hot oil and continue frying the rosettes until the batter is finished.
instructions.11: Periodically remove any fried bits from the oil. Add more oil as needed.
instructions.12: If the rosettes are browning too quickly and burning, reduce the heat of the oil.
instructions.13: Once cooled, transfer the rosettes to a serving platter and dust with powdered sugar and, if desired, pistachios and crushed rose petals.

w-ir-019.culturalNotes: Persian Rosettes (nan panjareh) are a traditional Iranian sweet served on special occasions and celebrations.

w-ir-020.title: Nan-e Berenji (Persian Rice Cookies)

instructions.1: Using an electric mixer, beat the butter and powdered sugar until the mixture is light and fluffy.
instructions.2: Add one egg yolk and mix to combine. Then, add the second yolk and beat again.
instructions.3: Add the rosewater, ground cardamom, and rice flour. Mix with a spatula until the dough comes together. Be careful not to overmix.
instructions.4: Wrap the dough in plastic wrap and refrigerate it for 4 to 6 hours.
instructions.5: Preheat your oven to 350°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Bring the dough out of the fridge and let it sit at room temperature for 30 minutes so it's easy to form.
instructions.6: Scoop out ½ tablespoon of dough, roll it into a smooth ball, and gently flatten it between your palms. Avoid pressing with your fingers or a cup to prevent cracking.
instructions.7: Use the edge of a spoon to create light indentations on the surface. Sprinkle poppy seeds on top for a decorative touch.
instructions.8: Bake for 18 minutes or until the edges turn slightly golden brown.
instructions.9: Let the cookies cool completely before touching or transferring them.

w-ir-020.culturalNotes: Nan-e Berenji is a traditional Iranian cookie made from rice flour and flavored with rosewater and cardamom.

w-ir-021.title: Persian Chickpea Cookies (Nan-e Nokhodchi)

instructions.1: Mix the canola oil with powdered sugar, cardamom, and rose water.
instructions.2: Add the roasted chickpea flour and mix well.
instructions.3: Transfer the dough to a clean work surface lined with a piece of plastic wrap. Gently bring the dough together using your hands.
instructions.4: Press the dough with your hands to form a flat rectangle. Wrap it in the plastic wrap and let it rest at room temperature for 4 hours.
instructions.5: Preheat the oven to 300 degrees F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
instructions.6: Roll the dough between two sheets of plastic wrap to a thickness of about 1/2 inch. Cut out the cookies using a small cookie cutter. Using a butter knife, lift the cookies and place them on the baking sheet.
instructions.7: Bake the cookies for 15 minutes. Let them cool completely before moving them to the serving plate.

w-ir-021.culturalNotes: Nan-e Nokhodchi is a traditional Iranian cookie, often served on special occasions.

w-ir-022.title: Persian Spinach and Eggs (Nargesi)

instructions.1: Heat the olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Saute the onion until translucent.
instructions.2: Add the garlic and spinach. You might need to add the spinach in two batches. Cook until the spinach is wilted and the excess liquid is evaporated. Add the turmeric, salt, and pepper.
instructions.3: Using a spoon, make wells in the pan and crack the eggs into the wells.
instructions.4: Cover with a lid and cook for 3 to 8 minutes, until the eggs are done to your liking.
instructions.5: Serve warm.

w-ir-022.culturalNotes: Nargesi is a traditional Iranian dish often served as a breakfast or light lunch.

w-ir-023.title: Salad Olivieh (Persian Potato Salad with Chicken)

instructions.1: Wash and peel the potatoes, then cut them into quarters. Place the potatoes in a large saucepan and cover with water. Add the eggs to the potatoes and bring to a boil.
instructions.2: Once boiling, reduce the heat to medium and continue cooking until the potatoes are fork-tender. Drain the water and transfer the potatoes to a large mixing bowl to cool. Set the eggs in a cold water bath to cool.
instructions.3: While the eggs and potatoes are cooling, heat 1 tablespoon of extra virgin olive oil in a small pan over medium-high heat.
instructions.4: Season both sides of the chicken breast with 1/2 teaspoon of salt. Once the oil is hot, add the chicken breast. Cook until the chicken breast is browned, then flip over and cook the other side. Reduce the heat to low and add 2 tablespoons of lemon juice.
instructions.5: Cover the pan and continue cooking until the chicken is thoroughly cooked and the juices run clear, about 15 minutes. Remove the chicken from the heat and let it cool.
instructions.6: When the potatoes are cool to the touch, coarsely cut them into 1/2-inch pieces in the mixing bowl. Peel the cooked eggs, dice them, and add them to the potatoes.
instructions.7: Dice the cooled chicken breast and add it to the mix.
instructions.8: Add the diced pickles, peas, 1/2 teaspoon of salt, and 1/4 teaspoon of black pepper to the potato mix and stir to combine.
instructions.9: Stir in the mayonnaise, 2 tablespoons of lemon juice, and 2 tablespoons of olive oil into the potato salad until smooth.
instructions.10: Cover and refrigerate the salad olivieh until ready to serve.
instructions.11: When ready to serve, transfer the salad olivieh to a serving plate and shape it into a round mound. Garnish as desired with sliced radishes, green onions, and fresh herbs. Serve alone or with lavash.

w-ir-023.culturalNotes: Salad Olivieh is a popular salad in Iran, often served at special occasions and family gatherings.

w-ir-024.title: Qottab

instructions.1: Mix the yogurt and baking powder in a bowl and set aside.
instructions.2: Mix the melted butter with the egg yolks. Add the yogurt and stir to combine.
instructions.3: Add the flour and mix using a spatula and then your hands to bring the dough together. Make sure not to over-knead the dough.
instructions.4: Wrap the dough in plastic and refrigerate for one hour.
instructions.5: For the filling: Grind the walnuts and mix with powdered sugar, rosewater, and ground cardamom. Stir well.
instructions.6: Roll out the dough and cut into circles. Place a spoonful of the filling in the center of each circle and fold to form a half-moon shape.
instructions.7: Grease a baking sheet and place the qottab. Bake in a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F) for 15 minutes until golden brown.
instructions.8: Dust the qottab with powdered sugar before serving.

w-ir-024.culturalNotes: Qottab is a traditional Iranian sweet typically served on special occasions.

w-ir-025.title: Persian Ice Cream with Saffron and Rose Water

instructions.1: Allow the ice cream to soften at room temperature for 10 minutes.
instructions.2: In the meantime, combine the saffron and hot water in a small bowl.
instructions.3: When the ice cream has softened, place it in a large bowl and mix in the saffron mixture, rose water, and pistachios until thoroughly combined.
instructions.4: Scrape the ice cream back into its original container and freeze until hardened, at least 6 hours.

w-ir-025.culturalNotes: Persian ice cream with saffron and rose water is a traditional dessert in Iran, often served on special occasions.

w-ir-026.title: Sabzi Polo

instructions.1: Wash the rice in warm water three times to remove starch and grit.
instructions.2: Soak the rice in water after washing.
instructions.3: Mix hot water with crushed saffron and let it steep for 10 minutes.
instructions.4: Mix the chopped herbs and reserve.
instructions.5: Add 1/2 teaspoon of salt to 8 cups of water and bring to a boil.
instructions.6: Add the drained rice to the boiling water and cook for 6 minutes until it floats to the surface.
instructions.7: Strain the rice and return the pot to medium heat and add olive oil.
instructions.8: Arrange the potato slices on the bottom of the pot and sprinkle 1/4 teaspoon of salt.
instructions.9: Add the drained rice over the potatoes and spread it evenly.
instructions.10: Add a spoonful of the herb mixture over the rice and repeat the layers until finished.
instructions.11: Pour the saffron mixture and 1 tablespoon of olive oil over the rice.
instructions.12: Cover the pot with a clean towel and cook for 10 minutes on medium heat, then lower the heat and cook for 45 minutes.
instructions.13: Serve the rice on a platter and add the tahdig (crust) on the side.

w-ir-026.culturalNotes: Sabzi Polo is a main dish in Iranian cuisine, often served with fish on special occasions.

w-ir-027.title: Persian Sweet Rice (Shirin Polo)

instructions.1: Wash the rice in a medium-sized bowl with water. Gently wash the rice by stirring it in the water with your hand to remove some of the starch and grit. Pour out the water and repeat two more times.
instructions.2: After washing and draining the rice a third time, cover the rice again with water and stir in 1 tablespoon of salt.
instructions.3: In a small bowl, mix hot water and saffron. Set aside to steep.
instructions.4: Fill a 5-quart non-stick pot with 8 cups of water and 1 tablespoon of salt. Bring the water to a boil.
instructions.5: When the water has come to a boil, pour out the water in the bowl containing the soaking rice. Add the wet rice to the boiling water.
instructions.6: When the water comes to a boil again and the rice floats to the top of the pot (approximately 6 minutes), pour the contents of the pot through a fine colander. The rice is ready to strain if you bite a rice kernel and the center is still uncooked.
instructions.7: Return the pot to the burner, set the heat to medium, and add olive oil. Arrange the potato slices in a single layer on the bottom of the pot.
instructions.8: Using a spatula, gently scoop the drained rice into the pot. Do not push the rice together as this will result in mushy rice. Scatter the rice throughout the pot in a pyramid shape until finished. The pot should not be filled to the top. Leave about 3 inches between the top of the rice and the top of the pot.
instructions.9: Using the handle of a long wooden spoon or another utensil, gently press a hole down the center of the rice to allow steam to travel freely through the pot.
instructions.10: Scatter 2 tablespoons of butter pieces along the top of the rice.
instructions.11: Cover the lid of the pot with a clean towel or several paper towels, and set it firmly over the pot to prevent steam from escaping. The towel will keep condensation from dropping back into the rice and turning it into mush.
instructions.12: After 7 minutes, lower the heat to low and let the rice finish cooking for another 45 minutes.
instructions.13: While the rice is cooking, prepare the toppings.
instructions.14: Using a sharp knife or peeler, remove the skin from the oranges. Remove the pith, the white part of the skin, from the peel and cut it into thin strips about 1 inch long.
instructions.15: In a small pan over medium heat, add orange peels and 1/4 cup of water with 1 tablespoon of sugar. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to medium-low. Cook until syrupy, about 15 minutes. Remove from heat and reserve.
instructions.16: Cut carrots into matchstick-size strips. In a small pan over medium heat, add carrots and 1 tablespoon of butter.
instructions.17: When the carrots soften, about 5 minutes, stir in 1 tablespoon of sugar and cinnamon.
instructions.18: Cook for another 5 minutes and stir in 1/2 teaspoon of the saffron water. Remove carrots from heat and reserve.
instructions.19: In a small pan, dry toast nuts over medium heat until toasted. Remove from heat and reserve.
instructions.20: In a small pan over medium heat, combine 1 tablespoon of butter and raisins. Cook for 3 minutes, then stir in 1/2 teaspoon of the saffron water. Reserve the raisins.
instructions.21: When the rice is done steaming, scoop out a spatula-full of rice and place it in a small bowl. Stir in the remaining saffron water and mix until the rice is uniformly golden.
instructions.22: Using a spatula, remove the remaining rice and scatter it onto your serving platter. Top with the saffron rice. Place the crunchy potatoes around the rice or serve on a separate plate.
instructions.23: Scatter the reserved candied carrots, candied orange peel, raisins, almond, and pistachio slivers over the top of the rice.

w-ir-027.culturalNotes: Shirin Polo is a traditional sweet rice dish in Iranian cuisine, often served on special occasions and celebrations.

w-ir-028.title: Mango Sorbet (Dessert)

instructions.1: Cut the mangoes: Place a mango on the cutting board with the stem side down. Using a sharp knife, cut from the top of the mango down one side of the pit. Repeat on the other side.
instructions.2: Score the flesh of the mango into a checkerboard pattern with a knife, without cutting through the peel. Use a spoon to scoop out the segments.
instructions.3: Add the mango pieces to a blender with the remaining ingredients. Blend until completely smooth.
instructions.4: Pour the mixture into a freezer-safe bowl and cover. Every 30 minutes for 4 hours, stir the sorbet very well with a whisk or a hand blender.
instructions.5: Let the sorbet freeze for 8 hours or until hard.

w-ir-028.culturalNotes: Sorbet is a type of cold dessert served in Iran, especially on hot days.

w-ir-029.title: Persian Tahchin

instructions.1: Mix the ground saffron with 2 tbsp of hot water and set aside.
instructions.2: In a small bowl, combine 1/2 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1/2 tsp dried parsley, 1/4 tsp garlic powder, and 1/8 tsp black pepper. Season both sides of each chicken breast.
instructions.3: Heat a pan over medium-high heat and add 1 tsp of extra virgin olive oil. When the oil is hot, add the chicken breasts. Cook the chicken until browned, about 5 minutes.
instructions.4: Flip the chicken over and brown the other side. Reduce the heat and add 2 tbsp of lemon juice. Cover the pan and cook until the chicken is done, about 10 minutes.
instructions.5: Remove the chicken from the heat and shred it with two forks. Add 1 tsp of saffron water to the chicken juices in the pan and mix with the shredded chicken. Reserve.
instructions.6: Wash the rice with water and soak it for 30 minutes. Rinse the rice again with water. Repeat this process two more times.
instructions.7: After washing the rice for the third time, rinse and soak it in water with 1 tbsp of salt.
instructions.8: In a 5-quart non-stick pot, add 8 cups of water and 1 tbsp of salt and bring to a boil. When the water has come to a boil, pour out the water in the bowl containing the soaking rice. Add the wet rice to the boiling water.
instructions.9: When the water boils again and the rice floats to the top of the pot (about 6 minutes), pour the contents of the pot into a fine colander. Ensure the rice is still uncooked in the center. Allow the rice to cool slightly before mixing with yogurt and eggs.
instructions.10: Preheat the oven to 500°F.
instructions.11: In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the yogurt and egg yolks until smooth. Stir in the remaining saffron water. Add the drained and cooled rice and gently mix until all the rice is coated.
instructions.12: Grease the bottom and sides of a 9x13 Pyrex pan with 1 tbsp of butter.
instructions.13: Spread half of the rice mixture evenly into the bottom of the pan.
instructions.14: Spread the shredded chicken over the rice layer.
instructions.15: Top with the remaining half of the rice mixture.
instructions.16: Cover with foil and place in the oven. If you like your tahchin crispy, reduce the heat to 450°F and bake for 30 minutes, then reduce to 350°F and bake for 1 hour. If you do not want it crispy, reduce the heat to 400°F and bake for 30 minutes, then reduce to 350°F and bake for 1 hour. Rotate the dish halfway through the cooking time to ensure even browning.
instructions.17: Right before serving, heat a small pan over medium-high heat. Melt 1 tbsp of butter then add the barberries and sugar. Once the sugar is mixed and combined, remove from heat.
instructions.18: To serve, remove the foil and place a large serving platter over the rice. Carefully invert and remove the pan. Top with chopped pistachios, almond slivers, and barberries.

w-ir-029.culturalNotes: Tahchin is a main dish in Persian cuisine, often served on special occasions and family gatherings.

w-ir-030.title: Yazdi Cake

instructions.1: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Line a muffin tin with liners.
instructions.2: In a large bowl, whisk eggs and sugar together until fully combined.
instructions.3: Add Greek yogurt, vegetable oil, ground cardamom, and rose water. Mix well.
instructions.4: In another bowl, whisk flour, cornstarch, and baking powder together.
instructions.5: Add half of the flour mixture to the egg-wet ingredients. Whisk well.
instructions.6: Add the rest of the flour mixture. Mix until combined.
instructions.7: Using an ice cream scoop, fill the muffin liners. Top with sesame seeds.
instructions.8: Bake in the oven for 8 minutes at 400°F. Then reduce the heat to 350°F and bake for another 10-12 minutes until the muffins are golden brown and a toothpick inserted in the muffins comes out clean.
instructions.9: Once baked, take the muffins out of the oven, let cool for 15 minutes, and serve with your favorite beverage!

w-ir-030.culturalNotes: Yazdi cake is a traditional dessert from the city of Yazd in Iran, known for its unique flavor of cardamom and rose water.

w-ir-031.title: Zereshk Polo with Chicken

instructions.1: Prepare the liquid saffron by mixing the ground saffron with ice cubes until dissolved.
instructions.2: In a small bowl, mix the tomato paste with salt, pepper, and turmeric.
instructions.3: In a large pot, heat the oil and butter, then add the chicken and brown on all sides.
instructions.4: Add the sliced onion, bell pepper, and carrots, and sauté for 5 minutes.
instructions.5: Add the tomato paste mixture, liquid saffron, and water, then bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer for 30 minutes.
instructions.6: In another pot, prepare the Persian rice according to the usual recipe.
instructions.7: In a small pot, heat the oil and add the barberries, sugar, and water, and bring to a boil for 5 minutes.
instructions.8: When the rice is ready, place the chicken and vegetables on top of the rice, then add the barberries.
instructions.9: Cover the pot and cook on low heat for 10 minutes.
instructions.10: Serve the dish hot.

w-ir-031.culturalNotes: Zereshk Polo with Chicken is a main dish in Iranian cuisine, often served on special occasions and family gatherings.

w-my-001.title: Nyonya Acar Fish

w-my-001-i2.name: silver mullet or bone-in Red Snapper fish fillet

instructions.1: Dry the turmeric, ginger, and garlic under the sun for a few hours.
instructions.2: Marinate the fish with some salt before deep-frying until golden and crispy.
instructions.3: Transfer the fish to a deep pot, followed by the ginger, garlic, and chilies.
instructions.4: Heat a wok and stir-fry the turmeric until the oil turns yellow. Discard the turmeric using a colander.
instructions.5: Add water and vinegar to the wok and bring it to a boil. Season with sugar and salt to taste.
instructions.6: Transfer the marinade into the pot, ensuring that the fish and ingredients are submerged.
instructions.7: Sprinkle sesame seeds on top, cover the pot, and let the fish pickle overnight.
instructions.8: The fish is best served the next day.

w-my-001.culturalNotes: Nyonya Acar Fish is a traditional dish in Malay cuisine, known for its spicy and tangy flavor.

w-my-002.title: Ayam Masak Merah

w-my-002-i10.name: vegetable oil
w-my-002-i10.standardAmount: for deep frying + ¼ cup extra

instructions.1: Rub the chicken with turmeric and salt, and set aside for 30 minutes.
instructions.2: Heat oil in a wok and deep fry the chicken pieces until golden brown. Set aside.
instructions.3: Roughly chop the red onion, ginger, galangal, and lemongrass, then transfer them to a blender or food processor. Add the chilies and garlic, and process into a paste.
instructions.4: Heat the wok with ½ cup of oil. Sauté the spices—cinnamon, star anise, cloves, and cardamom—until fragrant. Add the blended paste and increase the heat until it bubbles. Then, reduce the heat and simmer until the paste is fully cooked, fragrant, and the oil separates from the paste (pecah minyak).
instructions.5: Add the canned tomato soup, coconut milk, and chicken pieces. Raise the heat to bring it to a quick boil, then reduce to a simmer and cook until the sauce thickens. Season with salt to taste and garnish with spring onions before serving.

w-my-002.culturalNotes: Ayam Masak Merah is a traditional Malaysian dish featuring chicken in a spicy tomato sauce.

w-my-003.title: Bubur Cha-Cha

w-my-003-i14.name: banana
w-my-003-i14.standardAmount: 3 bananas (peeled and cut half inches thick)

instructions.1: In boiling water, cook the black-eyed peas until soft. In a separate pot, boil the sago until translucent and cooked through. Set aside.
instructions.2: Peel and cut the sweet potatoes and yam into cubes or desired shapes. Steam each type separately until soft.
instructions.3: To make the tapioca jelly, mix the flour with ½ cup boiling water until a dough forms. Once cool, roll out on a floured surface and cut into small cubes. Boil the jelly pieces in water until they float and become chewy, then drain and set aside.
instructions.4: In a separate pot, bring 1 liter of water to a boil. Add 1 tablespoon sugar and the banana slices. Boil for 5 minutes, then drain and set aside.
instructions.5: In a large pot, bring 1.5 to 2 liters of water to a gentle boil (start with less if you prefer a thicker texture). Add the thick coconut milk, sugar, salt, and pandan leaves. Simmer on low heat for 10–15 minutes, stirring occasionally. Taste and adjust the coconut milk or sugar if needed.
instructions.6: Add the black-eyed peas, sago, steamed sweet potatoes, yam, banana, and cooked tapioca jelly into the coconut milk base. Stir gently to combine and heat through. Serve hot or cold, based on your preference.

w-my-003.culturalNotes: Bubur Cha-Cha is a traditional Malaysian dessert soup served as a light meal or dessert. It is characterized by its sweet and tangy flavors and varied textures.

w-my-004.title: Air Fryer Char Siu Chicken

instructions.1: Marinate the chicken with 75 ml of Char Siu Sauce for at least 30 minutes.
instructions.2: Place the chicken skin side down in the air fryer basket. Spoon over half of the leftover marinade and air fry at 190°C (375°F) for 10 minutes.
instructions.3: Flip the chicken, spoon over the remaining marinade, and air fry at 190°C (375°F) for 4 minutes or until cooked through and slightly charred.
instructions.4: Garnish with sesame seeds and serve with steamed white rice.

w-my-004.culturalNotes: Air Fryer Char Siu Chicken is a popular dish in Malaysian cuisine, typically served with steamed white rice.

w-my-005.title: Coconut Jam (Seri Kaya)

instructions.1: Crack the eggs into a large bowl, then add the coconut milk and sugar. Whisk well by hand.
instructions.2: Strain the mixture into a non-stick saucepan and add the pandan leaves. Cook on low heat, stirring continuously for about 20 minutes. Add the cornstarch mixture to thicken the coconut jam. Turn off the heat and discard the pandan leaves.
instructions.3: In another saucepan, heat the sugar over medium-high heat until it melts into caramel. Once it turns golden brown, remove from heat and add it to the kaya and stir well. The kaya should turn golden brown.
instructions.4: Transfer the kaya to a blender and blend until smooth and lump-free. Spread on toast to make kaya toast. Store the leftover in a jar in the fridge for up to a week.

w-my-005.culturalNotes: Seri Kaya is a coconut jam commonly used in Malaysia to make kaya toast.

w-my-006.title: Curry Puff (Karipap)

instructions.1: Blend the dried red chilies, shallots, and curry powder in a food processor until smooth.
instructions.2: Heat the oil in a pot and sauté the curry leaves, chilies, and shallots until the shallots turn golden.
instructions.3: Add the chicken, potatoes, yellow onions, and water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes until the chicken and potatoes are tender.
instructions.4: Add salt and sugar to taste and cook for an additional 5 minutes.
instructions.5: Let the filling cool, then chill it in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.
instructions.6: In a bowl, mix the flour, butter, and ghee (if using) to make the oil dough.
instructions.7: In another bowl, mix the flour and water to make the water dough.
instructions.8: Roll the oil dough inside the water dough to create the spiral pastry shell.
instructions.9: Cut the dough into small pieces and roll them to form the pastry shells.
instructions.10: Fill the pastry shells with the filling, then fold and shape them.
instructions.11: Bake the puffs in a preheated oven at 180°C for 20-25 minutes until golden brown.

w-my-006.culturalNotes: Curry puffs are a popular dish in Malaysia, also known as karipap. They are served as a snack or appetizer.

w-my-007.title: Devil's Curry (Kari Debal)

instructions.1: Soak the dried red chilies in water for 20-30 minutes, then coarsely chop the shallots and garlic, and mince the lemongrass, ginger, and galangal. Combine all the ingredients in a blender and puree until smooth. Set aside.
instructions.2: In a heavy pot, heat the oil over medium heat. Add the mustard seeds and cook until they start to pop.
instructions.3: Add the spice paste to the oil and fry until aromatic, about 10 minutes, or until the oil separates and floats to the top.
instructions.4: Add the chicken and stir to coat it with the spice paste. Let it cook for about 8-10 minutes, then add the potatoes and stir to combine.
instructions.5: Pour in the water, ensuring it barely covers the chicken and potatoes. Add salt and sugar to taste. Stir well and bring to a boil. Then, reduce the heat to a simmer, cover with a lid, and let it simmer for about 20-30 minutes, or until the potatoes are soft.
instructions.6: Adjust the seasoning with salt and sugar. Add the white vinegar or tamarind juice and stir to mix well. Turn off the heat and serve the Devil’s Curry garnished with cilantro, if using. Serve hot with steamed rice.

w-my-007.culturalNotes: Devil's Curry is a spicy and distinctive dish from Malaysian cuisine, known for its strong flavor and rich spices.

w-my-008.title: Dosa (Indian-style Pancakes)

instructions.1: Mix the brown rice flour and whole wheat flour in a large bowl.
instructions.2: Gradually add the water to make a thin batter.
instructions.3: Add the onion, garlic, cilantro, sugar, turmeric, cumin, mustard seeds, cumin seeds, coriander, ginger, cayenne pepper, and rice vinegar, and mix well.
instructions.4: Cover the batter and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes or overnight.
instructions.5: To cook the dosas, heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat.
instructions.6: Pour 1/4 cup of batter into the skillet and spread it over the bottom in a thin layer.
instructions.7: Cook for 1 minute, then flip and cook for 1 minute more.
instructions.8: Remove the dosa from the pan and repeat with the remaining batter.

w-my-008.culturalNotes: Dosa is a popular breakfast dish in India and South Asia, typically served with chutneys and vegetables.

w-my-009.title: Gulai Tumis (Tamarind Fish Curry)

instructions.1: Heat the oil over low heat and sauté the ground spice paste until the oil separates from the paste and it becomes fragrant (about 15 minutes).
instructions.2: Mix the tamarind pulp with water and strain to extract the tamarind juice. Add the juice to the spice paste and bring to a boil over low heat. Simmer for about 10-15 minutes.
instructions.3: Add the ginger flower and fish. Simmer for 5 minutes or until the fish is cooked through.
instructions.4: Serve with lady's fingers.

w-my-009.culturalNotes: Gulai Tumis is a traditional Malaysian dish known for its spicy and sour flavors. It is usually served with rice.

w-my-010.title: Hainanese Chicken Rice

w-my-010-i17.name: chili sauce
w-my-010-i17.standardAmount: 3 tablespoons (Huy Fong brand Chili Garlic Sauce)

w-my-010-i18.name: garlic
w-my-010-i18.standardAmount: 15 g (peeled and grated, or finely minced)

w-my-010-i19.name: ginger
w-my-010-i19.standardAmount: 50 g (peeled and grated, or finely minced)

instructions.1: Wash the chicken thoroughly and prepare the ginger and scallions. Place the chicken in a large pot with the ginger, scallions, and salt. Add water and bring to a boil over medium heat. Reduce heat and simmer for 30 minutes.
instructions.2: Remove the chicken from the broth and immerse it in ice cold water for 10 minutes. Cut the chicken into pieces and let it cool.
instructions.3: In another pot, heat the vegetable oil and sauté the garlic and shallots until golden. Add the rice, broth, and salt, and bring to a boil. Reduce heat and cook for 20 minutes until the rice is tender.
instructions.4: In a small bowl, mix the vegetable oil, garlic, shallots, chicken fat, light soy sauce, chicken broth, and sesame oil. Mix well.
instructions.5: In another bowl, mix the garlic, ginger, salt, sugar, chicken broth, and lime juice. Mix well.
instructions.6: Serve the rice with the sliced chicken, sauces, cucumber, and cilantro.

w-my-010.culturalNotes: Hainanese chicken rice is a popular dish in Malaysia, also known as Nasi Ayam Hainan. It is typically served at special occasions and for lunch.

w-my-011.title: Kuih Kosui

instructions.1: In a pot, dissolve the sugar in 450 ml of water over low heat until the sugar is fully dissolved. Set aside to cool.
instructions.2: Cut the pandan leaves into small pieces. Combine the leaves and 600 ml of water in an electric blender and blend for 1-2 minutes. Strain the pandan juice through a fine sieve, then add the lye water (kansui) to the juice. Set aside.
instructions.3: In another bowl, combine the rice flour and tapioca flour. Slowly pour in the pandan juice mixture while stirring continuously until well blended. Then, add the sugar syrup.
instructions.4: Cook the flour mixture over low heat until slightly thickened. Remove from heat and pour the mixture into small tea cups. Steam the Kuih Kosui on high heat for 15 minutes. Remove the Kuih Kosui immediately after steaming.
instructions.5: Let the Kuih Kosui cool at room temperature for at least 6 hours before removing them from the tea cups. To serve, add freshly grated coconut on top of the Kuih Kosui.

w-my-011.culturalNotes: Kuih Kosui is a traditional Malaysian dessert usually served on special occasions.

w-my-012.title: Angku Kuih (Red Tortoise Cake)

w-my-012-i13.name: banana leaf
w-my-012-i13.standardAmount: 1 leaf (cut into rectangle to fit the angku mould)

instructions.1: Soak the split green beans for 6 hours, then wash them thoroughly.
instructions.2: Add the soaked green beans, fine sugar, and oil to a blender and blend until smooth.
instructions.3: Strain the mixture and transfer it to a bowl.
instructions.4: Add the orange coloring and mix well.
instructions.5: In another bowl, mix the wheat starch, boiling water, sugar, glutinous rice flour, mashed orange sweet potato, water, and cooking oil until the mixture is smooth.
instructions.6: Bring water to a boil in a pot and gradually add the mixture, stirring constantly until it becomes thick and cohesive.
instructions.7: Wash the banana leaf and cut it into rectangles to fit the angku molds.
instructions.8: Lightly oil the angku molds and fill them with the mixture.
instructions.9: Place the molds in a steamer over boiling water and steam for 15-20 minutes until cooked.
instructions.10: Let them cool slightly before serving.

w-my-012.culturalNotes: Angku Kuih is a traditional cake in Malaysia, often served on special occasions and celebrations.

w-my-013.title: Coconut Sticky Rice in Banana Leaves | Lemang

instructions.1: Soak the rice in water for at least 6 hours or overnight.
instructions.2: Bring coconut milk to a simmer for 15-20 minutes until the coconut oil separates from the milk.
instructions.3: Add the rice to the coconut milk and cook over low/medium heat for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
instructions.4: Cut banana leaves into 4-inch wide strips. You can soften them by quickly passing them over an open flame.
instructions.5: Form the banana leaves into cone shapes, ensuring there is no hole at the bottom.
instructions.6: Stuff the banana leaf cones with rice (leaving about 1.5 inches from the top). Pack it down tightly with the back of a spoon.
instructions.7: Fold the sides in, like when wrapping a present.
instructions.8: Layer each cone into a steamer basket, pressing the folded edge against the sides of the steamer to keep packets shut. Steam for 20 minutes, or until the rice is tender.

w-my-013.culturalNotes: Lemang is a traditional dish in Malaysia, often served during celebrations and festivals.

w-et-001.title: Ethiopian Coffee Ceremony

instructions.1: Wash the coffee beans in cool water and pick through them to remove any unsuitable beans.
instructions.2: Pour off the excess water and roast the beans in a pan over medium/medium-low heat until they start popping and turn dark brown. Stir continuously with a wooden skewer or keep shaking the pan.
instructions.3: Grind the roasted beans. In urban parts of Ethiopia, coffee grinders are used, but you can grind them by hand if you prefer.
instructions.4: Add one tablespoon of coffee grounds for each cup of water and brew the coffee in a jebena (a special clay coffee pot) or any other pot.
instructions.5: Pour the coffee into small cups from a height of about 8-10 inches to create a beautiful stream of dark coffee.
instructions.6: Serve the coffee with plenty of sugar and a smile, and you can also serve popped popcorn as a side.

w-et-001.culturalNotes: The Ethiopian coffee ceremony is an important part of Ethiopian culture, often served during various social gatherings.

w-et-002.title: Ful Medames

instructions.1: Add the onion, tomatoes, and fava beans to a medium pot.
instructions.2: Add water to almost cover the ingredients.
instructions.3: Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook for about 45 minutes or until the flavors meld nicely.
instructions.4: Mash or puree the beans.
instructions.5: Season with salt, then drizzle with lemon juice, olive oil, and a healthy handful of chopped parsley.
instructions.6: Serve the ful medames hot with chopped hard-boiled eggs and pita bread.

w-et-002.culturalNotes: Ful medames is a traditional breakfast dish in Ethiopia, often served with hard-boiled eggs and pita bread.
