w-et-003.title: Ethiopian Spiced Bread (Himbasha)

instructions.1: Knead all ingredients together until smooth.
instructions.2: Cover and let rise in a warm spot for 45 minutes to 1 hour or until doubled in size.
instructions.3: Roll out the dough thinly to fill an oiled, 12-inch oven-safe pan or skillet - about 1/3 inch thick.
instructions.4: Immediately cut with a ravioli wheel.
instructions.5: Let rise 30-45 minutes - until puffed and doubled in size.
instructions.6: Preheat the oven to 350F.
instructions.7: Brush with oil and bake for 15-20 minutes.

w-et-003.culturalNotes: Himbasha is a traditional Ethiopian spiced bread known for its rich flavors. It is typically served with main meals or as a snack.

w-et-004.title: Injera (Ethiopian Teff Flatbread)

instructions.1: Mix the flour with the water and salt. Add the fermentation starter if using.
instructions.2: Set aside to ferment for at least 12 hours, or overnight. Bubbles should appear on the surface.
instructions.3: Heat a large, flat pan until it is hot enough to make a droplet of water sizzle.
instructions.4: Lightly oil the pan.
instructions.5: Pour some batter onto the pan, spiralling outwards from the center. The batter should be a little thicker than a crêpe.
instructions.6: As it cooks, the surface of the injera will become covered in holes or pits. When the entire injera has changed color and the edges start to lift from the pan, remove it and set aside.
instructions.7: Repeat until all the batter is used up.

w-et-004.culturalNotes: Injera is a traditional Ethiopian flatbread used as a base for many Ethiopian dishes.

w-et-005.title: Niter Kibbeh (Ethiopian Spiced Clarified Butter)

instructions.1: Toast the whole spices in a dry skillet over medium heat for a few minutes until very fragrant. Be careful not to scorch the spices or they will become bitter. Set aside.
instructions.2: Place all the ingredients in a medium saucepan and bring it to an extremely low simmer. Continue to simmer over low heat for at least one hour or up to 90 minutes. Be very careful not to burn the butter or it will become bitter.
instructions.3: Pour everything through a fine-mesh cheesecloth. No need to skim off the foam, everything will be removed during straining. Pour the niter kibbeh into a jar, let it cool, and cover so that it is airtight. It will keep at room temperature for several weeks, in the fridge for a few months, and even longer in the freezer (it will be hard in the fridge and freezer, let it come to room temp for easy scooping).

w-et-005.culturalNotes: Niter kibbeh is a spiced clarified butter used in Ethiopian cuisine to enhance the flavor of dishes.

w-id-025.title: Gado-gado (Indonesian Salad with Peanut Sauce)

w-id-025-i8.name: fresh lime juice or rice vinegar

instructions.1: Fry the terasi in vegetable oil until fragrant.
instructions.2: Fry the peanuts until golden brown. Remove from the pan and let cool, then drain off the excess oil.
instructions.3: Grind the peanuts to a paste.
instructions.4: Add ground chili pepper, garlic, salt, sugar, and terasi to the peanut paste. Grind to mix.
instructions.5: Put the peanut paste in a pan, and add water to dissolve (use coconut milk for a richer taste).
instructions.6: Add additional sugar to the peanut sauce to taste, and bring to a boil.
instructions.7: Simmer the peanut sauce until thick, and season with the lime juice or vinegar.

w-id-025.culturalNotes: Gado-gado is a traditional Indonesian salad, typically served with a spicy and sweet peanut sauce.

w-id-026.title: Grass Jelly (Cincau)

w-id-026-i5.name: cold milk (or soy milk or any milk of your choice)

w-id-026-i10.name: cubes or strips of mango or other fresh fruit of your choice

instructions.1: In a bowl, mix the grass jelly powder with 4 cups of water.
instructions.2: Bring the mixture to a boil over medium heat, stirring constantly for 10 minutes until the powder is fully dissolved.
instructions.3: Add the sugar and palm sugar, and stir well for 5 minutes until the sugar is dissolved.
instructions.4: Pour the mixture into a tray or cups, and let it cool for 15 minutes, then refrigerate for 2 hours until set.
instructions.5: To make the palm sugar syrup: Mix 1/3 cup of palm sugar with 1/3 cup of water, and bring to a boil for 5 minutes until it becomes a syrup.
instructions.6: To make the grass jelly drink: Mix grass jelly cubes with cold milk and palm sugar syrup to taste.
instructions.7: To make the grass jelly dessert: Mix grass jelly cubes with condensed milk, coconut milk, sweetened red bean, palm seeds, and mango to taste.

w-id-026.culturalNotes: Cincau is a popular drink and dessert in Indonesia, served cold in glass cups.

w-id-027.title: Gudeg (Yogyakarta Gudeg)

instructions.1: Place all the ingredients for the ground spices in a food processor and process into a paste. Add a little bit of water if needed to get it going.
instructions.2: Preheat a large pot or dutch oven with cooking oil. Add the ground spices and bay leaves and saute until fragrant, about 5 minutes.
instructions.3: Add the chicken, jackfruit, and red beans and stir to mix. Pour in the coconut milk, tea bag, salt, and brown sugar. Bring it to a boil and then lower the heat and cover to let it cook for the next 1 hour.
instructions.4: Uncover and then add in the hard-boiled eggs and let it cook again for another hour or so until the jackfruit is soft to the point where you can easily shred it with a fork. The beans should be soft and chicken meat is almost falling off the bones. The liquid should be almost all absorbed at this point and the eggs are nicely tinted with brown color.

w-id-027.culturalNotes: Gudeg is a traditional dish from Yogyakarta, Indonesia, typically served with rice and sambal.

w-id-028.title: Chocolate Sprinkles on Bread (Hagelslag)

instructions.1: Spread the slice of bread with softened butter.
instructions.2: Sprinkle the chocolate sprinkles over the buttered bread.
instructions.3: Serve and enjoy!

w-id-028.culturalNotes: Hagelslag is a popular Dutch breakfast dish that spread to Indonesia during the colonial period.

w-id-029.title: Grilled Fish in Spicy Padang Sauce

instructions.1: Marinate the fish in a mixture of lime juice, coriander powder, salt, and white pepper for 15 minutes.
instructions.2: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F).
instructions.3: In a bowl, blend the red chili, Thai chili, garlic, shallots, ginger, galangal, turmeric, kaffir lime leaves, bay leaves, lemongrass, sugar, salt, and white pepper until smooth.
instructions.4: Place the fish in a baking dish and cover with the spicy sauce.
instructions.5: Brush the fish with oil and grill for 10 minutes on each side, or bake in the oven for 20 minutes.
instructions.6: Serve the grilled fish hot with the spicy sauce.

w-id-029.culturalNotes: Grilled fish in spicy Padang sauce is a famous dish in Indonesian cuisine, especially in the Padang region.

w-id-030.title: Kastengel (Dutch-Indonesian Cheese Tarts)

instructions.1: Mix the butter with the egg yolk until well combined.
instructions.2: Add the grated cheese, flour, milk powder, and chicken powder. Mix the ingredients well to form a dough.
instructions.3: Cover the dough and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
instructions.4: Shape small pieces of the dough and place them on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
instructions.5: Brush the dough with the egg yolk and sprinkle grated cheese on top.
instructions.6: Bake the Kastengel in a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F) for 20 minutes or until golden brown.
instructions.7: Let them cool before serving.

w-id-030.culturalNotes: Kastengel is a popular Dutch-Indonesian cookie, often served on special occasions.

w-id-031.title: Karedok

instructions.1: Cut the cucumber, cabbage, eggplant, long beans, and bean sprouts and place them in a large salad bowl.
instructions.2: Use a food processor to blend the dressing ingredients into a paste. You may need a little water to help the process.
instructions.3: Before serving, pour the dressing over the salad and toss to mix everything well.

w-id-031.culturalNotes: Karedok is a traditional vegetable salad from West Java, Indonesia, known for its sweet and sour dressing.

w-id-032.title: Ketoprak (Indonesian Vermicelli Tofu Salad)

instructions.1: Blanch the dry rice stick noodles briefly in hot water until they soften but are not mushy. Drain and then refresh with cold water. Set aside.
instructions.2: Peel the cucumber and cut it in half lengthwise. Use a spoon to scoop out the seeds, then cut it into 1-inch slices.
instructions.3: Prepare the peanut dressing: Crush the garlic and red chilis in a bowl. Add the roasted peanuts, brown sugar, tamarind paste, and warm water. Mix well until the dressing is smooth.
instructions.4: Cut the tofu into small cubes and fry in vegetable oil until golden brown. Drain and set aside.
instructions.5: In a large bowl, mix the noodles, bean sprouts, cucumber, hard-boiled eggs, and fried shallots. Add the peanut dressing and mix well.
instructions.6: Serve the ketoprak in serving dishes and top with prawn crackers.

w-id-032.culturalNotes: Ketoprak is a popular dish in Indonesia, often served as a snack or light lunch.

w-id-033.title: Ketupat and Lontong (Rice Cakes)

instructions.1: Rinse the rice in several changes of water and then completely drain off the water.
instructions.2: Use the cup that comes with the rice cooker, or any other cup for measuring, but make sure you use the same one to measure the rice and the liquid.
instructions.3: Add the rice, water, and salt to the rice cooker or Instant Pot.
instructions.4: Pressure Cook on the Instant Pot for 10 minutes, then let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes.
instructions.5: Or use the Rice function on the Instant Pot for 20 minutes.
instructions.6: Mold the cakes into ketupat or lontong shapes.

w-id-033.culturalNotes: Ketupat and lontong are types of rice cakes common in Indonesia, often served with sauces and meats.

w-id-034.title: Keripik Kentang Balado

instructions.1: Cut the potatoes into thin slices and soak them in water for 10 minutes.
instructions.2: Drain the potatoes and fry them in cooking oil until they turn golden brown and crispy.
instructions.3: In another pan, heat 50 grams of cooking oil and fry the minced shallots until they turn golden brown.
instructions.4: Add the kaffir lime leaves, bay leaves, Thai chili, sambal oelek, sugar, apple cider vinegar, and galangal powder. Cook the mixture for 5 minutes over low heat.
instructions.5: Add the fried potatoes to the sambal and mix well.
instructions.6: Serve the keripik hot or cold as desired.

w-id-034.culturalNotes: Keripik is a popular crispy snack in Indonesia, often served as an appetizer or with light meals.

w-id-035.title: Kue Bangkit Santan

instructions.1: Wash the pandan leaves and cut them into 3-4 inch pieces.
instructions.2: Place the pandan leaves in a bowl and cover with water. Soak for 30 minutes.
instructions.3: Strain the pandan leaves and place them in a blender with 100 ml of coconut cream. Blend until smooth.
instructions.4: Strain the mixture through a fine sieve to obtain a clear liquid.
instructions.5: In a bowl, mix the pre-cooked tapioca flour with icing sugar and salt (if using).
instructions.6: Add the pandan and coconut cream mixture to the flour and mix well until the dough is smooth.
instructions.7: Test the dough to ensure it is not too dry or too wet. If it is dry, add more coconut cream. If it is too wet, add more flour.
instructions.8: Dip a small spoon in hot water and shape the dough into small discs.
instructions.9: Place the discs on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
instructions.10: Bake the cookies in a preheated oven at 150°C for 15-20 minutes until golden brown.
instructions.11: Remove the cookies from the oven and let them cool before serving.
instructions.12: You can add a few drops of red food coloring if desired.

w-id-035.culturalNotes: Kue Bangkit is a traditional Indonesian sweet often made for special occasions such as Eid.

w-lb-001.title: Akkawi Cheese Manakeesh

instructions.1: Add the lukewarm water to a bowl, then add the yeast and stir well. Let it sit for 5 minutes until it starts to bubble.
instructions.2: Mix the flour, salt, and sugar in a large bowl.
instructions.3: Gradually pour the yeast water and oil into the dry ingredients. Stir well to bind, then knead for 5 to 10 minutes until the dough is smooth and elastic.
instructions.4: Place the dough in a large bowl greased with oil. Cover the dough with a damp tea towel and let it rise in a warm place for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until doubled in size.
instructions.5: Meanwhile, crumble the akkawi cheese into a large bowl. Cover it with cold water to help remove the salt.
instructions.6: Punch down the dough. Divide the dough into four equal-sized pieces.
instructions.7: Place the dough back into the bowl and let it rest for an extra 30 minutes.
instructions.8: Preheat the oven to 450 F.
instructions.9: On a floured surface, roll each ball of dough into a disc about 10 inches in diameter.
instructions.10: Drain the akkawi cheese. Sprinkle about 1 cup of akkawi cheese over the dough. Sprinkle about 1/2 tablespoon of nigella seeds evenly over the cheese.
instructions.11: Transfer the dough to a cookie sheet or pizza stone and bake for 20 minutes, or until the crust is baked and the cheese is melted.

w-lb-001.culturalNotes: Manakeesh is a traditional dish in Lebanon, often served as a breakfast meal.

w-lb-002.title: Baba Ghanoush

instructions.1: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F).
instructions.2: Wrap the eggplant in aluminum foil and roast for 45-60 minutes until it is soft when poked with a fork or knife. Unwrap the eggplant and let it cool for 10 minutes.
instructions.3: When the eggplant is cool to the touch, cut off the top and peel off the skin. Keep only the flesh of the eggplant.
instructions.4: Place the eggplant flesh in a food processor. Add the lemon juice, tahini, garlic cloves, and salt. Pulse a few times until the ingredients are incorporated but the mixture still looks chunky.
instructions.5: Serve the baba ghanoush with olive oil, pomegranate seeds, and pita chips.

w-lb-002.culturalNotes: Baba ghanoush is a popular dish in Lebanese and Arab cuisine, served as a dip with Arabic bread.

w-lb-003.title: Balela Salad

instructions.1: In a large bowl, whisk together the lemon juice, olive oil, cumin, salt, and black pepper.
instructions.2: Add the red onion to the dressing and stir to coat. Let sit for 5 minutes to mellow the onion while you prepare the rest of the ingredients.
instructions.3: Add the chickpeas, tomatoes, green bell pepper, parsley, and mint on top of the dressing and onions.
instructions.4: Gently stir until everything is evenly coated. Let rest another 5 minutes before serving.

w-lb-003.culturalNotes: Balela is a traditional Lebanese salad served as an appetizer or light meal. It is known for its refreshing and healthy flavor.

w-lb-004.title: Shish Barak

instructions.1: Prepare the dough. In the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the hook attachment, mix the flour, water, olive oil, and salt until it forms a smooth, springy ball, 5 to 7 minutes. Cover and allow the dough to rest at room temperature for 30 minutes.
instructions.2: Make the beef filling. Heat the olive oil in a medium size pan over medium heat. Add the ground beef and onions, and cook, breaking up the ground beef with the back of a spatula until it is minced and browned, about 10 minutes. Add the garlic, season with 7 spice, salt and pepper, and cook until fragrant, 2 more minutes. Fold in the parsley and pine nuts. Set aside.
instructions.3: Cut the dough. Lightly flour a flat surface and use a rolling pin to roll the dough flat about ⅛-inch in thickness, about 16x16 inches wide. Use a small 2-inch cookie cutter or round object to cut the dough into discs. You can roll the remaining dough pieces and make more discs from it.
instructions.4: Make the dumplings. Preheat the oven to 425°F and line a large baking sheet with parchment paper. Add about 1 teaspoon of the beef filling into the piece of dough and fold over into a half moon shape. Pinch the two ends together to close into a tortellini shape. Place on the prepared baking sheet. Repeat with the remaining dough and filling. Bake in the preheated oven until the dumplings are lightly browned, about 15 minutes. Set aside.
instructions.5: Prepare the yogurt sauce. Whisk together the yogurt, water, cornstarch, salt, and dried mint in a large pot with no heat until there are no more clumps. Once the mixture is well combined, turn the heat to medium and stir frequently until the mixture starts to thicken, about 10 minutes. It will continue to thicken as it cooks with the dumplings.
instructions.6: Assemble and serve. Add the baked dumplings into the yogurt sauce and cook until the dumplings start to float to the top, about 10 minutes. Ladle the dumplings with the sauce into bowls, garnish with pine nuts and mint. Serve hot.

w-lb-004.culturalNotes: Shish Barak is a traditional dish in Lebanese cuisine, often served on special occasions.

w-lb-005.title: Batata Harra

instructions.1: Arrange an oven rack in the middle position. Line a baking sheet with foil and place it in the oven. Preheat the oven and the baking sheet to 500°F.
instructions.2: Peel the potatoes and cut them into 1-inch cubes. Place the potatoes in a medium bowl and toss with 1 tablespoon of olive oil, 1/2 teaspoon of salt, and 1/4 teaspoon of red pepper flakes.
instructions.3: Remove the hot baking sheet from the oven and place the potatoes on it in a single layer, ensuring the potato cubes are not touching each other. Return the pan to the oven and roast for about 20-25 minutes.
instructions.4: Meanwhile, in a medium serving dish, whisk to combine the remaining olive oil, salt, garlic, and red pepper flakes, and half of the chopped cilantro.
instructions.5: When the potatoes are done, transfer them from the hot pan to the serving dish and toss with the oil mixture. Dust with the remaining cilantro and serve immediately.

w-lb-005.culturalNotes: Batata Harra is a popular dish in Lebanese cuisine, served as an appetizer or alongside main dishes.

w-lb-006.title: Air Fryer Green Beans

instructions.1: Prepare the green beans by trimming their stems and cutting larger ones in half if needed.
instructions.2: Place the green beans in a large bowl with olive oil, salt, and pepper. Toss to combine.
instructions.3: Transfer the green beans to the air fryer and shake the basket to ensure they are in a single layer. You may need to cook in batches.
instructions.4: Cook the green beans until crisp-tender, shaking the basket halfway through, for 8-10 minutes.
instructions.5: Squeeze fresh lemon juice on top and serve immediately.

w-lb-006.culturalNotes: Green beans are a common dish in Lebanese cuisine, often served as an appetizer or part of a main meal.

w-lb-007.title: Air Fryer Bread

instructions.1: In a large bowl, combine the flour, yeast, salt, warm water, olive oil, and honey until a slightly shaggy, sticky dough forms.
instructions.2: Knead the dough with your hands until it forms a soft ball.
instructions.3: Cover the dough with a kitchen towel or plastic wrap and let it rise in a warm place for 50-60 minutes until it doubles in size.
instructions.4: Prepare a large piece of parchment paper large enough to lift the bread in and out of the air fryer. Lightly dust your hands with flour and shape the risen dough into a smooth ball.
instructions.5: Transfer the shaped dough to the parchment paper. Cover and let it rise again for about 15 minutes.
instructions.6: During the second rise, preheat the air fryer to 400°F and remove the basket if possible.
instructions.7: After rising, use a sharp knife to make a ½-inch deep cut on top of the dough. Carefully transfer the parchment paper and dough into the hot air fryer basket.
instructions.8: Cook the bread for 5 minutes at 400°F, then reduce the temperature to 350°F and continue cooking for 15 minutes.
instructions.9: Carefully lift the parchment paper and the bread out of the air fryer and use tongs to flip the loaf. Then, lift the parchment paper and bread back into the air fryer to continue cooking for 15 more minutes.
instructions.10: Once done cooking, tap the bottom of the loaf to check for doneness. It should sound hollow.
instructions.11: Carefully remove the parchment paper and loaf and allow to cool completely before slicing, about 45 minutes.

w-lb-007.culturalNotes: Bread in Lebanon is a staple of the culinary culture and is served with many traditional dishes.

w-lb-008.title: How to Cook Bulgur Wheat

instructions.1: In a small pot, combine the fine bulgur wheat (No. 1), 2 cups of water, and ½ teaspoon of salt. Bring to a boil over medium heat.
instructions.2: Once boiling, reduce the heat and simmer for 10 minutes.
instructions.3: Remove from heat and let the bulgur sit for 5 minutes.
instructions.4: Drain the bulgur and let it cool slightly before using.
instructions.5: To cook medium or coarse bulgur, combine the bulgur, 1.5 cups of water, and ½ teaspoon of salt in a pot.
instructions.6: Bring to a boil over medium heat, then reduce the heat and simmer for 15 minutes.
instructions.7: Remove from heat and let the bulgur sit for 10 minutes.
instructions.8: Drain the bulgur and let it cool slightly before using.

w-lb-008.culturalNotes: Bulgur is a staple in Lebanese cuisine and is used in many dishes such as kibbeh and tabbouleh.

w-lb-009.title: Cabbage Roll Soup

instructions.1: In a heavy-bottomed pot, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the diced onions and cook for 5-6 minutes until softened.
instructions.2: Add the garlic, thyme, salt, and pepper, and cook until the garlic is fragrant, about 1 minute.
instructions.3: Add the ground beef and cook, breaking it up with a spoon, until browned and no longer pink, about 6-8 minutes.
instructions.4: Add the chopped cabbage, crushed tomatoes, Worcestershire sauce, and vegetable broth. Bring to a boil and then stir in the uncooked rice.
instructions.5: Reduce the heat to a simmer and cook uncovered for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the rice and cabbage are tender. Serve hot.

w-lb-009.culturalNotes: This soup is a popular dish in Lebanese cuisine and is typically served on cold days.

w-lb-010.title: Almond Cake

instructions.1: Preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Grease a 9-inch round cake pan and line the bottom with parchment paper.
instructions.2: In a medium bowl, mix together the almond flour, semolina flour, baking powder, and salt. Set aside.
instructions.3: In a large bowl, beat together the butter and 1 cup of granulated sugar until pale and fluffy. Beat in the eggs, milk, and almond extract, then fold in the flour mixture just until combined.
instructions.4: Transfer the batter into the prepared cake pan, smoothing with a spatula to even out. Sprinkle the slivered almonds and remaining tablespoon of granulated sugar over the top.
instructions.5: Bake in the preheated oven for 30 minutes, or until golden brown and firm in the center, and a cake tester comes out clean.
instructions.6: Let cool completely in the pan before slicing and serving.

w-lb-010.culturalNotes: Almond cake is a popular dessert in Lebanese cuisine, often served on special occasions and holidays.

w-lb-011.title: Chili Powder

instructions.1: Chop the dried red chiles and remove the seeds.
instructions.2: Grind the chiles in a spice grinder until finely ground, about 1 minute.
instructions.3: Stir in the cumin, paprika, Mexican oregano, garlic powder, and cayenne pepper with the ground chiles.
instructions.4: Store the chili powder in an airtight container.

w-lb-011.culturalNotes: Chili powder is a fundamental spice in Mexican and Lebanese cuisine, used in many recipes to add a spicy and aromatic flavor.

w-lb-012.title: Chocolate Dipped Candies

instructions.1: Line two sheet pans with waxed paper.
instructions.2: Place the nuts, dried fruit, and other inclusions in small bowls, each with its own teaspoon.
instructions.3: Temper the chocolate: Melt the chocolate gently in the microwave (15-second increments, stir between) or over a barely simmering double boiler, very slowly, to 110 degrees. Cool down by seeding the melted chocolate with more finely chopped chocolate and stirring frequently until it reaches 84 degrees. Warm back up very gently to 89-91 degrees and keep the chocolate at that temperature for dipping.
instructions.4: Dip the candies: Work swiftly to keep the chocolate tempered, at 88-91 degrees throughout this process. Pour about a cup of chocolate over the nuts or other inclusions in one of the small bowls set up earlier. Stir until coated. Using a teaspoon, drop a small quantity (4-5 almonds, for example) onto the waxed paper, arranging the nuts on top of one another to form the piece of candy. Repeat until all of the inclusion is dipped. Repeat this process for each bowl of inclusions, dipping one bowl of inclusions at a time before pouring chocolate into the next bowl.
instructions.5: If the chocolate cools too much and goes out of temper (it thickens), place it back on the double boiler or in the microwave at five-second intervals to bring it back to temperature (88-91 degrees) and continue working.
instructions.6: Place the sheet pans of candies in a cool, dry spot to set up and harden. Box for gifts, or place in little paper cups on a platter or tiered plate stand to serve, extra special.

w-lb-012.culturalNotes: Chocolate-dipped candies are a traditional Lebanese confection, often given as gifts on special occasions.

w-lb-013.title: Avocado Chicken Salad Croissant Sandwich

instructions.1: In a large mixing bowl, mash half the avocados. Add the Greek yogurt, Dijon mustard, garlic (if using), lemon juice, and lemon zest. Whisk together until well combined (or blend in a blender or food processor for a smoother consistency).
instructions.2: Add the chicken, celery, green onions, salt, and black pepper on top and stir to combine.
instructions.3: Cover the mixture and store in the fridge for at least 4 hours to set.
instructions.4: When ready to serve, fold in the remaining chopped avocado and top with fresh cilantro, if using.
instructions.5: Serve the avocado chicken salad in a croissant or on whole grain bread.

w-lb-013.culturalNotes: The croissant is a famous French pastry that has become a part of daily Lebanese cuisine, especially for breakfast.

w-lb-014.title: Air Fryer Falafel

instructions.1: Cover the chickpeas with water in a large bowl. Set aside at room temperature to soak for 12-24 hours until they double in size.
instructions.2: Drain the chickpeas, rinse, and dry them thoroughly.
instructions.3: Place the chickpeas and salt in the bowl of a food processor. Pulse until they form fine crumbles. Add the cilantro, parsley, onion, garlic, salt, cumin, coriander, crushed red pepper, and black pepper. Blend until the mixture turns into a thick green paste, scraping down the sides as needed. Remove the blade from the bowl, then cover the bowl and refrigerate for 1 hour.
instructions.4: Remove the falafel batter from the fridge. Sprinkle the baking powder over the top, then gently fold it throughout.
instructions.5: Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Set aside.
instructions.6: Using a small spoon or your hands, shape about 1.5 tablespoons of the batter into a round ball and place it on the parchment-lined baking sheet. Repeat with the remaining batter.
instructions.7: Heat the air fryer to 400°F. Arrange about 12 falafel balls in the air fryer basket, spray the balls with cooking spray, and cook for 10 minutes until golden brown and puffed. Repeat with the remaining falafel balls to make about 36.
instructions.8: Transfer the falafel to a serving platter and serve with tahini sauce for dipping.

w-lb-014.culturalNotes: Falafel is a popular dish in Arabic cuisine, especially in Lebanon, where it is served as an appetizer or a light meal.

w-lb-015.title: Cheese Fatayer

w-lb-015-i6.name: olive oil
w-lb-015-i6.standardAmount: ¼ cup (plus more for oiling the bowl)

instructions.1: In a large bowl, mix the flour, yeast, sugar, and salt. Add the warm water and olive oil and knead the ingredients until the dough is smooth and elastic.
instructions.2: Cover the dough and let it rest for 30 minutes until it rises.
instructions.3: In another bowl, mix the mozzarella cheese, feta cheese, parsley, and black pepper.
instructions.4: Divide the dough into small balls. Roll out each ball using a fork or your fingers to make it thin.
instructions.5: Place a spoonful of the cheese mixture in the center of each dough piece. Seal the fatayer tightly.
instructions.6: Place the fatayer on a baking sheet greased with oil. Bake in a preheated oven at 180°C for 20 minutes until golden brown.

w-lb-015.culturalNotes: Fatayer are traditional pastries in Lebanese cuisine, served as a light snack or for breakfast.

w-lb-016.title: Fatteh with Chickpeas

instructions.1: In a small saucepan over high heat, add the chickpeas, water, garlic, cumin, salt, and pepper. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer for 15 minutes. Add the tahini and use a potato masher to lightly mash some of the chickpeas while keeping most of them whole. Cover to keep warm until ready to serve.
instructions.2: In a large non-stick skillet over medium heat, add the pine nuts and dry toast for 5 minutes, until golden brown. Set aside in a small bowl.
instructions.3: Add 1 tablespoon of olive oil and the pita bread pieces to the same skillet over medium heat. Toast for 8-10 minutes, stirring frequently, until golden brown and crispy. Set aside in a medium bowl.
instructions.4: Lower the heat to medium-low. Add the remaining tablespoon of olive oil to the skillet along with the garlic and salt. Cook until the garlic is fragrant, about 1 minute. Pour the yogurt on top of the garlic and stir gently until the yogurt becomes warm and loosens, being careful not to let the yogurt boil, about 5 minutes.
instructions.5: When ready to serve, transfer the chickpea mixture to a round serving dish and pour the yogurt sauce over the chickpeas. Add the toasted pita on top, followed by the toasted pine nuts, and garnish with parsley. Serve immediately.

w-lb-016.culturalNotes: Fatteh with chickpeas is a traditional dish in Lebanese cuisine, often served as a main course during family gatherings.

w-lb-017.title: Fattoush

w-lb-017-i15.name: Pita bread
w-lb-017-i15.standardAmount: 1 large double ply pita bread (cut into triangles)

instructions.1: Make the Dressing: Whisk together the lemon juice, garlic, sumac, pomegranate molasses, dried mint, salt, and black pepper in a bowl. Slowly stream in the olive oil while whisking continuously until emulsified.
instructions.2: Fry the Pita Bread: In a large skillet, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the pita bread and stir frequently until golden and crispy, about 5-7 minutes. Set aside.
instructions.3: Prepare the Salad: Place the lettuce, tomatoes, cucumbers, green peppers, green onions, and parsley in a large serving bowl. Pour the dressing over the ingredients and toss to combine.
instructions.4: Add the fried pita bread to the salad just before serving.

w-lb-017.culturalNotes: Fattoush is a traditional Lebanese salad served as an appetizer in meals.

w-lb-018.title: Grilled Halloumi

instructions.1: Drain the halloumi and place it on a cutting board. Slice it into wide thin pieces, about 8 slices. Pat the slices very dry with paper towels.
instructions.2: Heat the oil in a grill pan or a non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Add the sliced halloumi in a single layer. Cook, undisturbed, until the bottoms are golden brown, 3 to 4 minutes.
instructions.3: Use a spatula to flip the halloumi and cook until the other side is also golden brown, 3 to 4 minutes longer. Transfer the halloumi to a plate; let cool for at least 5 minutes.
instructions.4: Plate the grilled halloumi with sliced tomatoes, sliced cucumbers, fresh mint, zaatar, and a drizzle of olive oil, if desired. Enjoy on its own or with pita bread.

w-lb-018.culturalNotes: Halloumi is a traditional cheese in Lebanon and the Middle East, known for its distinctive flavor and chewy texture, making it perfect for grilling.

w-lb-019.title: Kishk Soup

w-lb-019-i3.name: ground lamb or lean ground beef (optional)

instructions.1: In a medium saucepan over medium heat, melt the butter or heat the oil. Lower the heat and add the garlic, cooking just long enough to release the scent without browning it, about 1 minute.
instructions.2: Add the meat if using, and increase the heat to medium, stirring constantly to break up and brown the meat, about 5 minutes.
instructions.3: Add three cups of water to the pot. Gradually whisk in the kishk powder, a little at a time. Cook over medium-low heat until the mixture is thick, 5-10 minutes.
instructions.4: Ladle the soup into warm bowls and garnish with crushed dried mint. Serve with flatbread or pita.

w-lb-019.culturalNotes: Kishk is a traditional dish in Lebanese and Eastern cuisine, known for its rich flavor and high nutritional value.

w-lb-020.title: Kibbeh Nayyeh

instructions.1: Soak the bulgur in a small bowl with water for 15 minutes until the water is absorbed. Fluff the bulgur with a fork.
instructions.2: Place the ground beef, red pepper, butter, and salt in the bowl of a food processor. Blend until the meat forms a dough ball, stopping to scrape down the food processor as needed, about 5 minutes. Remove the mixture and place it in a large shallow bowl in the fridge.
instructions.3: In the same food processor, add the soaked bulgur, onion, kamouneh spice mixture, basil, and mint. Blend until well combined.
instructions.4: Transfer the bulgur kamouneh mixture on top of the meat paste, wet your hands with cold water, and knead the kamouneh mixture into the beef until well combined. Continue to add water to your hands while kneading until everything is well combined and smooth, about 5 minutes.
instructions.5: Transfer the kibbeh to a serving dish and spread it out to cover the surface of the plate. You can use a knife or fork to make designs across the kibbeh.
instructions.6: Garnish with fresh mint, drizzle with olive oil, and serve with pita bread.

w-lb-020.culturalNotes: Kibbeh nayyeh is a traditional dish in Lebanese cuisine, served as an appetizer or main course.

w-lb-021.title: Baked Kibbeh

w-lb-021-i1.name: olive oil
w-lb-021-i1.standardAmount: 2 tablespoons (plus more for greasing pan & drizzling on top)

instructions.1: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Grease a baking dish with olive oil.
instructions.2: In a bowl, mix the ground beef, diced onion, salt, 7 Spice, and pine nuts. Set aside.
instructions.3: In another bowl, mix the fine bulgur wheat, water, quartered onion, basil, mint, kamouneh spice, salt, and 7 Spice. Mix well until the ingredients are well combined.
instructions.4: Dip your hands in water and shape balls from the bulgur mixture. Fill each ball with the meat mixture and seal it well.
instructions.5: Arrange the kibbeh in the baking dish and drizzle with olive oil. Bake for 45 minutes or until golden brown.
instructions.6: Serve the kibbeh hot with toasted pine nuts.

w-lb-021.culturalNotes: Kibbeh is a traditional dish in Lebanese cuisine, often served on special occasions and family gatherings.

w-lb-022.title: Knafeh

instructions.1: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Grease an 11-inch round pan.
instructions.2: Make the simple syrup, combine the water, sugar, and lemon slices in a small saucepan over medium-high heat. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to a simmer, stirring occasionally until the sugar is dissolved and the mixture is thickened but still clear, about 5-7 minutes. Remove from heat, add the rose water, and set aside to cool.
instructions.3: Use a food processor to chop the shredded phyllo dough into smaller pieces. Transfer the phyllo dough into a large mixing bowl. Pour the butter into the bowl. Use your hands to mix the butter with the dough, rubbing handfuls of the dough between your palms.
instructions.4: In another large bowl, mix together the ricotta, mozzarella, and sugar.
instructions.5: Evenly spread the buttered phyllo dough into the prepared pan and firmly press it into the bottom and edges. Spread the cheese mixture onto the dough, leaving the edges around the pan empty.
instructions.6: Bake in the preheated oven until the cheese is slightly golden and the edges of the dough are brown and bubbly, 20 to 25 minutes.
instructions.7: Remove the Knafeh from the oven. Place a large platter or baking sheet over the baking dish. Using oven mitts, carefully invert the baking dish onto the platter so the phyllo is on top. Pour the syrup over the Knafeh. Cut into pieces and serve while hot.

w-lb-022.culturalNotes: Knafeh is a traditional dessert in Lebanon and the Middle East, often served on special occasions.

w-lb-023.title: Layali Lubnan

instructions.1: In a medium saucepan over medium heat, place the milk, semolina, and sugar. Stir frequently until the mixture is fully dissolved and creamy, about 20 minutes. Be careful not to let the milk boil.
instructions.2: Transfer the semolina pudding to an 8x11 baking dish and use the back of a spoon or spatula to spread the mixture to an even layer. Press a plastic wrap directly on the surface of the pudding to prevent a skin from forming and allow it to come to room temperature, about 15 minutes.
instructions.3: Remove the plastic wrap from the semolina pudding, spoon the ashta on top of the pudding, and sprinkle with pistachios all over. Cover lightly with plastic wrap, and allow the pudding to cool completely in the fridge, at least 2 hours.
instructions.4: When ready to serve, cut the pudding into 12 squares, and drizzle each serving with simple syrup.

w-lb-023.culturalNotes: Layali Lubnan is a traditional Lebanese dessert, often served on special occasions.

w-lb-024.title: Cheese Manakish

instructions.1: In a large bowl, mix the flour, yeast, and salt. Add the warm water and olive oil and knead the ingredients until the dough is smooth and elastic.
instructions.2: Cover the dough and let it rest for 30 minutes until it rises.
instructions.3: After the dough has risen, divide it into small balls and flatten each ball using a fork to make it thin.
instructions.4: Place the shredded cheese on the flattened dough.
instructions.5: Preheat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Bake the manakish for 10-15 minutes until golden brown.
instructions.6: Serve the manakish hot with labneh.

w-lb-024.culturalNotes: Manakish is a popular breakfast dish in Lebanon, often served with labneh and olives.

w-lb-025.title: Mezze Platter

instructions.1: Place the tabbouleh, hummus, baba ghanoush, and marinated olives into small bowls and arrange the bowls on a large platter or charcuterie board.
instructions.2: Arrange the cucumbers, tomatoes, and radishes on the platter.
instructions.3: Serve the mezze cold or at room temperature with warm pita for dipping.

w-lb-025.culturalNotes: Mezze is a selection of small dishes served as appetizers in Middle Eastern cuisine, and it is an essential part of meals in Lebanon.

w-lb-026.title: Muhallebi

instructions.1: In a small saucepan over medium heat, add the milk, sugar, and cornstarch, and stir well to combine all the ingredients.
instructions.2: Start whisking lightly but constantly as the mixture heats. It’s important not to stop whisking to avoid any clumps.
instructions.3: Once the mixture reaches a simmer, turn down the heat and continue whisking for about 5-7 minutes until the mixture thickens like pudding.
instructions.4: Stir in the rose water, then divide the pudding equally into eight cups or bowls.
instructions.5: Allow the containers to come to room temperature, then place them in the fridge for at least one hour to allow the pudding to set and chill.
instructions.6: Serve cold, garnished with pistachios and rose petals if desired.

w-lb-026.culturalNotes: Muhallebi is a traditional Lebanese dessert, often served on special occasions.

w-lb-027.title: Mujaddara

instructions.1: Rinse the lentils and wash them thoroughly. Fry the lentils in olive oil for 3-4 minutes, stirring continuously until some lentils show signs of scorching.
instructions.2: Add salt, baharat, cumin, and ground cardamom to taste.
instructions.3: Add 2 cups of water and cover the pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 20 minutes or until the lentils have absorbed all the water.
instructions.4: Fry the rice in olive oil for 3-4 minutes, stirring continuously until the grains change color.
instructions.5: Add salt, black pepper, and ground cardamom to taste.
instructions.6: Add 2 cups of water and cover the pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 5 minutes, then turn off the heat and let it stand for another 10 minutes.
instructions.7: Cut the onion into thin strips (about 0.5x4 cm / 0.2x1.6 in).
instructions.8: Fry the onion in olive oil until it is deeply golden brown and crispy (this may take a while but will result in much fuller flavor).
instructions.9: Mix the lentils and rice, and top with the fried onion. Use a 2:1 ratio of lentils to rice for a moist consistency.

w-lb-027.culturalNotes: Mujaddara is a popular dish in Lebanon and the Middle East, often served as a main course with a green salad.

w-lb-028.title: Qatayef

instructions.1: In a large blender, combine the flour, semolina, sugar, baking powder, instant yeast, salt, and warm milk. The consistency should be like very runny pancake batter.
instructions.2: Cover the batter with a towel and let it sit in a warm place for 30 minutes. Blend the mixture again and let it rest for 10 more minutes.
instructions.3: Meanwhile, make the simple syrup. Combine sugar and water in a small saucepan over medium-high heat. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat to medium and cook, stirring occasionally, until the sugar has dissolved, about 1-2 minutes.
instructions.4: Stir in the orange blossom water and lemon juice. Pour the syrup into a heatproof container and allow it to cool.
instructions.5: When the batter is done resting, heat a non-stick pan on medium heat, then pour 2 tablespoons of the batter onto the pan. You will notice the appearance of bubbles.
instructions.6: Cook until the bubbles dry out and the bottoms become golden, about 2 minutes. Do not flip. (If no bubbles are appearing, add more water or milk since your batter is probably too thick.) Set aside in a warm place covered so they remain moist.
instructions.7: Preheat the oven to 400°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper. In a small bowl, combine the ricotta, mozzarella cheese, and 2 tablespoons of the prepared simple syrup. Place a heaping tablespoon of the filling into each pancake and pinch the sides together.
instructions.8: Place the closed atayef on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, spray with cooking spray, and bake for 40 minutes, flipping halfway through.
instructions.9: Serve immediately, drizzled with simple syrup, if desired.

w-lb-028.culturalNotes: Qatayef is a traditional Arabic dessert, especially popular during Ramadan. It is usually served with syrup and cheese.

w-lb-029.title: Sayadieh

instructions.1: Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a large deep skillet over medium heat and fry the chopped onions until lightly golden brown, about 10-15 minutes.
instructions.2: Add the rice on top of the onions and season with 7 spice, ginger, cinnamon, cumin, turmeric, salt, and black pepper. Toss well to combine the rice with the spices and onions. Toast the rice lightly with the spices for about 5 minutes.
instructions.3: Add the water, bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover with a tight-fitting lid, and cook for 15 minutes. Remove from heat and let the rice rest, covered, for 10 more minutes. Uncover and fluff with a fork.
instructions.4: In a large non-stick skillet, heat the almonds and stir frequently until they are golden-brown and fragrant, 3 to 5 minutes. Transfer to a bowl and set aside.
instructions.5: Use paper towels to pat the cod fillets dry, then season with salt, black pepper, and cumin on both sides. Place the flour in a shallow bowl and dip the cod fillets lightly on both sides.
instructions.6: Heat the remaining 2 tablespoons of olive oil in the same skillet used to cook the almonds over medium-high heat.
instructions.7: Add the cod fillets to the skillet and cook the first side for about 3-4 minutes, then flip and cook the other side for about 3-4 minutes.
instructions.8: Serve the cooked fish on top of the rice mixture and garnish with toasted almonds and parsley.

w-lb-029.culturalNotes: Sayadieh is a traditional dish in Lebanese cuisine, often served on special occasions and family gatherings.

w-lb-030.title: Sfeha Flatbread

w-lb-030-i5.name: extra-virgin olive oil
w-lb-030-i5.standardAmount: 1/4 cup, plus more to coat the bowl

w-lb-030-i6.name: laban
w-lb-030-i6.standardAmount: 2 tablespoons, or plain whole milk yogurt

w-lb-030-i10.name: laban
w-lb-030-i10.standardAmount: 1 tablespoon, or plain whole milk yogurt

w-lb-030-i18.name: flatleaf parsley or mint leaves, or a combination, finely chopped

instructions.1: In a small bowl, stir the yeast with 1/4 cup of the warm water until dissolved. Set aside until creamy and frothy/bubbly, about 10 minutes.
instructions.2: In a mixing bowl, whisk the flour and salt. Slowly add the remaining 3/4 cup water, olive oil, yogurt, and proofed yeast mixture. Beat until a ball of dough forms, then increase speed to medium and knead for about 3 minutes, or 5 minutes by hand on the counter.
instructions.3: Coat another medium bowl lightly with olive oil. Place the dough in the bowl and cover with plastic wrap (not touching the dough). Cover with a kitchen towel and set aside to rise in a warm spot for 1 hour.
instructions.4: Meanwhile, in a medium bowl with clean hands, blend together the meat with the diced onion, pomegranate molasses, yogurt, tahini, tomato paste, garlic powder, salt, and cinnamon or 7 Spice.
instructions.5: Once the dough has risen, place one oven rack in the lower third of the oven and one in the upper third and heat the oven to 450° F. Line two sheet pans with parchment, silpats, or foil.
instructions.6: Divide the dough in half. Roll out one half at a time to 1/4-inch thickness. If cutting into 3-inch circles, cut out the circles, form a ball with the remainder and repeat with remaining dough.
instructions.7: Carefully transfer the larger or smaller dough circles to a lined sheet pan. Place tablespoons of the meat mixture around the top of the larger dough piece or just under a tablespoon per 3-inch circle.
instructions.8: Flatten, spread, and push the meat into the surface of the dough with your fingertips, reaching all the way to the very edge of the dough. Leave some spaces thin or somewhat free of the meat across the top.
instructions.9: Bake on the lower rack for about 7 minutes, then move to the top rack and broil on low for about 2 minutes, or until the dough is golden.
instructions.10: Remove from the oven to a cooling rack. Cover the top of the sheet pan with hot sfeha with a clean kitchen towel, to keep the sfeha soft.
instructions.11: To serve immediately, garnish with toasted pine nuts, pomegranate seeds, and chopped parsley. Cut the larger sfeha into square or pie pieces. To freeze, store in freezer bags, reheat wrapped in foil in a 300° F oven, and do not garnish until just before serving.

w-lb-030.culturalNotes: Sfeha is a traditional dish in Lebanese cuisine, served as a main course or as an appetizer.

w-lb-031.title: Sfouf (Turmeric Cake)

instructions.1: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Grease a 9×9-inch baking pan with the tahini.
instructions.2: In a large bowl, whisk together the semolina, flour, turmeric, and baking powder.
instructions.3: In a separate bowl, whisk together the sugar, milk, and oil until the sugar is dissolved and the mixture is well blended.
instructions.4: Pour the dry ingredients into the wet ingredients and stir until smooth and bright yellow.
instructions.5: Transfer the batter into the prepared pan and sprinkle the pine nuts over the top.
instructions.6: Bake for 30-35 minutes, until the top is set and lightly golden and the nuts are lightly golden but not brown.
instructions.7: Cool completely on a wire rack, then cut into 16 squares or diamond shapes.

w-lb-031.culturalNotes: Sfouf is a traditional Lebanese cake, known for its distinctive golden color from turmeric.

w-lb-032.title: Beef Shawarma

instructions.1: Prepare the marinade by whisking olive oil, vinegar, lemon juice, shawarma seasoning, and garlic in a large bowl until well combined.
instructions.2: Add the beef strips, sliced onions, and bay leaves to the bowl, and toss to fully coat the beef with the marinade. Let it sit in the fridge for 1-2 hours.
instructions.3: When ready to cook, transfer the beef to a bottom-heavy saucepan and cook until the beef is cooked through, about 8-10 minutes.
instructions.4: Prepare the tahini sauce by blending tahini paste, lemon juice, crushed garlic, and salt in a bowl or food processor. Slowly add water to reach the desired consistency.
instructions.5: Assemble the shawarma by placing the cooked beef in pita bread, drizzling with tahini sauce, and adding your choice of vegetables.

w-lb-032.culturalNotes: Shawarma is a popular dish in Lebanon and the Middle East, typically served in pita bread with tahini sauce and vegetables.

w-lb-033.title: Shish Kebab

instructions.1: Season the lamb cubes generously with salt and black pepper, then let them rest and come to room temperature.
instructions.2: Heat the grill to medium-high heat.
instructions.3: Thread the lamb, onion, and bell pepper pieces onto skewers, making sure not to pack them too tightly.
instructions.4: Brush the skewers with olive oil.
instructions.5: Place the skewers on the grill and cook for 10 minutes with the lid on, then flip and cook for another 10 minutes with the lid on.
instructions.6: Remove the skewers from the grill and let them rest for 10 minutes.
instructions.7: Remove the meat and vegetables from the skewers using a fork and serve.

w-lb-033.culturalNotes: Shish kebab is a popular dish in Lebanon and is often served at family gatherings and celebrations.

w-lb-034.title: Shish Taouk

w-lb-034-i7.name: Turkish Sweet Red Pepper Paste (Biber Salçası)

instructions.1: Make the marinade. In a large bowl, combine the olive oil, dried mint, crushed red pepper flakes, fresh thyme, Aleppo pepper, tomato paste, Turkish sweet red pepper paste, black pepper, and salt. Whisk to blend.
instructions.2: Marinate the chicken. Add the chicken pieces to the bowl with the marinade. Cover and let sit at room temperature for at least 30 minutes or, ideally, refrigerate overnight and then allow the chicken to come to room temperature before grilling.
instructions.3: Prepare the grill. Heat the rear element only of a gas grill to medium-high (about 400°F), creating both a hot direct-heat zone for searing and a cooler zone for more gentle cooking if needed.
instructions.4: Assemble the skewers. Remove the chicken from the marinade and thread the pieces onto skewers, leaving a small amount of space between each piece to encourage even cooking and browning.
instructions.5: Grill the chicken. Place the skewers over the hottest part of the grill and cook, turning every 3 to 4 minutes, until the chicken is lightly charred on all sides and cooked through, about 12 minutes total. If the outside is browning too quickly, move the skewers to the cooler side of the grill to finish cooking more gently. The chicken is ready when it reaches an internal temperature of 165°F.
instructions.6: Rest and serve. Transfer the skewers to a serving platter and let them rest for 3 to 5 minutes. Serve hot with tzatziki and steamed rice.

w-lb-034.culturalNotes: Shish Taouk is a traditional grilled dish in Lebanese cuisine, typically served with tahini and steamed rice.

w-my-014.title: Mee Goreng

instructions.1: Combine all the ingredients for the chili paste and blend well using a food processor.
instructions.2: Heat a wok and add the chili paste. Stir-fry until the oil separates from the chili. Set aside.
instructions.3: In a small bowl, combine all the ingredients for the sauce. Set aside.
instructions.4: Heat a wok on high heat and add 2 tablespoons of cooking oil. Add the garlic, 3 tablespoons of chili paste, potatoes, bean curd, and squid. Stir-fry until fragrant. Add the yellow noodles and the sauce, then continue stirring. Push the noodles to the side of the wok.
instructions.5: Add the remaining 1/2 tablespoon of cooking oil and crack the eggs on top of the oil. Scramble the eggs and mix them in with the noodles. Add the bean sprouts and stir quickly for about 1 minute.
instructions.6: Dish out the noodles and garnish with sliced lettuce leaves and lime wedges. Squeeze some lime juice over the noodles before serving.

w-my-014.culturalNotes: Mee Goreng is a popular dish in Malaysia, often served in restaurants and street food stalls.

w-my-015.title: Snow Skin Mooncake

instructions.1: Squeeze the juice and heat it until it reaches boiling point. Cool the juice in the fridge for about 4 to 6 hours.
instructions.2: Sift the powdered sugar and cooked glutinous rice flour. Add the shortening and combine until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs.
instructions.3: Add the juice and milk to the mixture, and mix until a soft and smooth dough forms. Let the dough rest for 10 minutes.
instructions.4: Divide the dough into 60 g (2 oz) portions and roll each portion into a ball. Wrap each ball with cling wrap until ready to use.
instructions.5: Fill each ball with the mooncake paste and wrap it well. Place the mooncakes in the fridge for 30 minutes before serving.

w-my-015.culturalNotes: Mooncakes are a traditional dessert served during the Mid-Autumn Festival in China and Malaysia.

w-my-016.title: Nasi Goreng (Fried Rice)

instructions.1: Break up the leftover rice using the back of a spoon to prevent clumping.
instructions.2: In a wok, toast the belacan over low heat until it is dry and aromatic. The toasted belacan should be powdery and resemble tiny granules.
instructions.3: Fry an egg until well-done and set aside.
instructions.4: Using a mortar and pestle or a mini food processor, blend the shallot, garlic, red chili, and toasted belacan. Transfer the blended paste to a small saucer.
instructions.5: Heat a wok and add oil. Add the flavoring paste and stir-fry until aromatic or until the oil separates.
instructions.6: Add the rice to the wok and mix well with the flavoring paste. Add kecap manis and palm sugar, continuing to stir-fry until everything is well blended.
instructions.7: Dish out the nasi goreng, top it with the fried egg, and serve immediately.

w-my-016.culturalNotes: Nasi Goreng is a popular dish in Malaysia and Indonesia, often served as a breakfast or dinner meal.

w-my-017.title: Nasi Lemak

w-my-017-i10.name: tamarind pulp
w-my-017-i10.standardAmount: size of a small ping pong ball

instructions.1: Rinse the rice with running tap water several times until the water turns clear. Drain the water completely.
instructions.2: Add 1.5 cups of water to the washed rice, followed by the coconut milk and a pinch of salt. Add the pandan leaves into the rice and cook the rice. Discard the pandan leaves after the rice is cooked.
instructions.3: Pound the shallots, garlic, dried chilies, and prawn paste with a mortar and pestle. Alternatively, you can grind them with a food processor.
instructions.4: Soak the tamarind pulp in water for 15 minutes. Constantly squeeze the tamarind to extract its flavor into the water. Drain the pulp and save the tamarind juice.
instructions.5: Rinse the dried anchovies with tap water a few times and let them drain. Heat 2 cups of oil in a pan, fry the anchovies until they've become light brown and crispy. Remove from oil with a strainer and drain on a paper towel-lined plate.
instructions.6: In a pan on medium to low heat, heat 2 tablespoons of frying oil. Stir-fry the spice paste until fragrant, turning reddish in color. Add the onion rings and fried anchovies, stirring well. Pour in the tamarind juice, salt, and sugar. Simmer on low heat until the sauce thickens. Set it aside.
instructions.7: Clean the small fish and season them with salt. Deep fry with the remaining frying oil.
instructions.8: To serve, scoop out a small bowl of rice and place it in the center of a plate. Arrange the fried fish, hard boiled eggs, roasted peanuts, and cucumber around the rice. Add 2 spoons of the sambal on top of the rice. Serve immediately.

w-my-017.culturalNotes: Nasi Lemak is a staple dish in Malaysian cuisine, typically served for breakfast or lunch.

w-my-018.title: Malaysian Herbed Rice Salad | Nasi Ulam

instructions.1: Bring water to a boil in a pot. Add salt and rice. Return to a boil, then cover and reduce heat to a simmer. Cook gently for about 16 minutes. Remove from heat and let steam for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork and let cool to room temperature.
instructions.2: Clean all herbs and pat dry. Slice and add to a bowl. Set aside.
instructions.3: Add all ingredients to a small bowl and stir to combine. Use chili peppers for heat, if desired.
instructions.4: When the rice has cooled, toss all ingredients together. Add dressing to taste. Taste it after 30 minutes and adjust seasonings if necessary.

w-my-018.culturalNotes: Nasi Ulam is a traditional Malaysian herbed rice salad, known for its variety of fresh herbs and spices.

w-my-019.title: Pineapple Tart (Tat nanas)

instructions.1: Cut the stalk off the pineapple and follow by the skin. Make sure all divits are removed. Slice the pineapple flesh into pieces and blend in a blender until they become puree.
instructions.2: Add the pineapple puree and cloves to a non-stick pot and cook on medium heat, constantly stirring to avoid burning.
instructions.3: When the pineapple is almost dry, add the sugar and lemon juice, stir to combine well. Lower the heat to simmer and continue to stir until the pineapple filling turns golden in color and becomes very sticky. Transfer the pineapple filling out, remove the cloves and chill in the fridge for 30 minutes.
instructions.4: Cream the butter and condensed milk until light and fluffy. Add in the egg yolk one at a time, and beat until well combined. Mix in the flour slowly to form the pastry dough. The dough is ready when it no longer sticks to your hands.
instructions.5: Prepare the egg wash by mixing all the ingredients together in a small bowl.
instructions.6: Divide the pineapple filling and dough into 100 portions. Roll them both into balls. To wrap, use your palms to roll each dough and then flatten it.
instructions.7: Add a pineapple ball in the middle and fold the edges of the dough up to cover the filling.
instructions.8: Finish it off by rolling it into a round ball.
instructions.9: Place the pineapple cookie on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Using the back of a paring knife, cut the criss-cross shape on the cookie, and brush the top of the cookie with the egg wash, twice. Repeat the same until all ingredients are used up.
instructions.10: Bake in a preheated oven at 330°F (165°C) for about 20-22 minutes or until they turn golden brown. Transfer them out and cool on a wire rack before storing in an airtight container.

w-my-019.culturalNotes: Pineapple tarts are a traditional dessert in Malaysia, often served during special occasions and celebrations.

w-my-020.title: Fried Popiah

instructions.1: In a wok, heat the cooking oil. Add the garlic and stir-fry until aromatic. Then, add the chicken, shrimp, and mushrooms, and continue to stir-fry until cooked.
instructions.2: Add the yam bean and carrot, and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes. Then, add 1 cup of water, cover with a lid, and simmer for 15-20 minutes until the vegetables are tender. Add the seasoning ingredients and mix well. Dish out and set aside.
instructions.3: Place a piece of spring roll wrapper on a flat surface. Add 2 spoonfuls of filling to the center of the wrapper, then fold in the two sides and roll it up. Use the flour mixture to seal the edges.
instructions.4: Heat a wok and pour in 2 cups of cooking oil. Deep fry the spring rolls over medium heat until golden brown and crispy. Remove them and drain on paper towels. Serve hot with chili sauce.

w-my-020.culturalNotes: Fried Popiah is a popular dish in Malaysia, also known as Popiah. It is typically served with chili sauce.

w-my-021.title: Rendang

instructions.1: Chop the lemongrass, ginger, galangal, garlic, onion, and Japanese chili peppers (if desired) and add them to the bowl of a food processor.
instructions.2: Blend into a fine paste.
instructions.3: Heat the coconut oil in a large wok and add the seasoning paste. Fry until fragrant and softened, 2-3 minutes.
instructions.4: Add the beef, coconut milk, water, sugar, and kaffir lime leaves. Stir and let simmer for about an hour.
instructions.5: As the liquid steams away, add the kerisik and cook for a few more minutes.
instructions.6: Serve with coconut sticky rice towers - Lemang.

w-my-021.culturalNotes: Rendang is a traditional dish from Malaysia and Indonesia, known for its rich flavors and coconut taste.

w-my-022.title: Roti Canai

instructions.1: Mix the flour, salt, and sugar in a large bowl.
instructions.2: Add the ghee, beaten egg, milk, and water, and mix the ingredients well until the dough is smooth and consistent.
instructions.3: Cover the dough and let it rest for 30 minutes.
instructions.4: Divide the dough into small balls.
instructions.5: Use a little ghee to roll each ball into a very thin circle.
instructions.6: Heat a skillet over medium heat and add a little ghee.
instructions.7: Place the thin circle in the skillet and cook until golden brown on both sides.
instructions.8: Repeat the process with the remaining dough.
instructions.9: Serve the roti canai hot with your favorite sauces.

w-my-022.culturalNotes: Roti canai is a popular flatbread in Malaysia, typically served with various sauces.

w-my-023.title: Soto Ayam

w-my-023-i3.name: chicken breast
w-my-023-i3.standardAmount: 1 skinless and boneless chicken breast (cut into cubes)

instructions.1: Soak the rice noodles in warm water to soften them. Set aside.
instructions.2: Blend the spice paste in a food processor, adding water if needed.
instructions.3: Add the oil to a pot over medium-high heat. Add the spice paste and stir until aromatic.
instructions.4: Add the chicken broth, coconut milk, lemongrass, and water. Bring to a boil. Add the chicken breast cubes, cover the pot, and simmer on low heat for 30 minutes. Add salt to taste.
instructions.5: Blanch the rice noodles, bean sprouts, and cabbage (if using) in another pot of boiling water. Transfer them to a bowl once cooked. Add the toppings of hard-boiled eggs and spring onions, then pour the hot chicken broth into the bowl.
instructions.6: Serve hot with lime wedges and shallot crisps on top of the noodles.

w-my-023.culturalNotes: Soto Ayam is a popular chicken soup in Malaysia, traditionally served in a wooden bowl.

w-ng-001.title: Akamu (Nigerian Pudding)

instructions.1: Fill a large bowl halfway with akamu lumps.
instructions.2: Crush the akamu lumps with a spoon into very small pieces. Mix in small amounts of cold water until the mixture is smooth and has the consistency of evaporated milk.
instructions.3: Bring a large pot of water to a boil.
instructions.4: Before the water boils, stir the mixture thoroughly. Once the water has reached a boil, carefully but steadily stir it into the akamu mixture. Stop stirring as soon as the mixture starts to set, and reduce the flow of water you're pouring to the bare minimum until the akamu has entirely set.
instructions.5: Thoroughly whisk the mixture. Add additional water as desired if the mixture is too thick.
instructions.6: Stir in evaporated milk and a pinch of sugar to taste.

w-ng-001.culturalNotes: Akamu is a traditional Nigerian breakfast dish, often served with groundnuts or fruits.

w-ng-002.title: Ofada Stew (Ayamase Stew)

instructions.1: Chop the onions.
instructions.2: Coarsely blend the green bell peppers, red bell pepper, and habanero peppers.
instructions.3: If the blended mix looks a bit watery, pour it into a pot and let it boil until some of the water evaporates.
instructions.4: Boil the beef with bouillon powder, black pepper, and salt until it is tender.
instructions.5: Bleach the palm oil (as outlined in the next section).
instructions.6: Add the onions, and after about a minute, add the blended pepper mix and iru.
instructions.7: Cook for about 5 minutes.
instructions.8: Add the beef and spices.
instructions.9: Cook for another 10 minutes on medium-low heat or until the oil begins to rise to the surface.

w-ng-002.culturalNotes: Ofada Stew is a popular dish in Nigeria, known for its rich and spicy flavors.

w-ng-003.title: Barbecued Meat

instructions.1: Add the beef to a large ziplock bag along with the lime juice, garlic powder, oregano, black pepper, and salt.
instructions.2: Seal the bag and mix the ingredients until they are evenly distributed. Marinate for at least 1 hour, or up to 5 hours for stronger flavor.
instructions.3: Grill the steak over medium heat until it reaches an internal temperature of 68-71°C (155-160°F), which is about medium. The cooking time will vary depending on the thickness of the steak.

w-ng-003.culturalNotes: Grilled meat is a popular dish in Nigeria, often served at special occasions and family gatherings.

w-ng-004.title: Ogbono Soup (Draw Soup)

instructions.1: If using whole ogbono seeds, grind them using a mortar and pestle or a coffee grinder. Skip this step if using pre-ground seeds.
instructions.2: In a large pot, add some palm oil on low heat and add the ogbono seeds.
instructions.3: Mix in the ogbono seeds and break any lumps with a serving spoon. Stir until it’s thoroughly coated.
instructions.4: Add the stock and stir. Add about a cup at a time until you reach your desired thickness. If you don't have enough stock, add water.
instructions.5: Bring to a boil, then set to low heat and let it cook for about 10 minutes, stirring intermittently.
instructions.6: Add the meats and spices.
instructions.7: Taste for salt and add some if needed.
instructions.8: If it becomes too thick, add a little more water.
instructions.9: Let simmer for about 10 minutes.
instructions.10: Add the chopped spinach and let simmer on low for about 2 more minutes.
instructions.11: Your ogbono soup is ready to serve!

w-ng-004.culturalNotes: Ogbono soup is a popular dish in Nigeria, often served with rice or fufu.

w-ng-005.title: Edikang Ikong (Nigerian Vegetable Soup)

instructions.1: Wash the goat meat thoroughly and cut it into small pieces. Place it in a pot and add 2 cups of water. Bring it to a boil over medium heat for 30 minutes until it is half-cooked.
instructions.2: Add the bouillon powder, black pepper, salt, and onion. Let it boil for 10 minutes.
instructions.3: Wash the waterleaf and ugwu leaves thoroughly and cut them into small pieces.
instructions.4: Add the waterleaf and ugwu leaves to the pot. Let them boil for 10 minutes.
instructions.5: Add the palm oil, smoked fish, shrimp, and ground crayfish. Let the mixture boil for 10 minutes.
instructions.6: Add the cayenne pepper and let the soup boil for 5 minutes.
instructions.7: Turn off the heat and serve the soup hot.

w-ng-005.culturalNotes: Edikang Ikong is a traditional Nigerian vegetable soup known for its rich flavor and green leaves.

w-ng-006.title: Efo Riro - Nigerian Spinach Stew

instructions.1: Wash the spinach thoroughly and chop it.
instructions.2: In a large pot, heat the palm oil over medium heat.
instructions.3: Add the chopped onion, habanero pepper, red bell pepper, and tomatoes, and stir for 5 minutes until the onion becomes translucent.
instructions.4: Add the cooked beef or goat meat and mushrooms, and continue stirring for 3 minutes.
instructions.5: Add the spinach, bouillon powder, ground crayfish, cayenne pepper, black pepper, and salt, and stir well.
instructions.6: Add the water or stock, bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat and let it simmer for 20 minutes.
instructions.7: Add the pepper flakes if desired, and continue cooking for an additional 5 minutes.
instructions.8: Serve the stew hot with rice or fufu.

w-ng-006.culturalNotes: Efo Riro is a popular dish in Nigeria, typically served with rice or fufu.

w-ng-007.title: Ewedu Soup

instructions.1: Wash the jute leaves thoroughly if using fresh, or let them thaw if using frozen.
instructions.2: Place the jute leaves in a pot and add enough water to cover them.
instructions.3: Add the ground crayfish, salt, iru (if using), pepper, and bouillon.
instructions.4: Bring the mixture to a boil over medium heat, then reduce the heat and simmer for 20-30 minutes until the leaves are tender.
instructions.5: Serve the soup hot with rice or fufu.

w-ng-007.culturalNotes: Ewedu is a traditional Nigerian soup often served with rice or fufu.

w-ng-008.title: Fried Plantain

instructions.1: Heat a thin layer of vegetable oil in a frying pan.
instructions.2: Meanwhile, cut the plantain into long, oblong slices.
instructions.3: Fry the slices in the oil on both sides until golden brown.
instructions.4: Sprinkle the fried plantain immediately with salt or brown sugar to taste.
instructions.5: Serve hot.

w-ng-008.culturalNotes: Fried plantain is a popular dish in Nigeria, served as a side or part of a main meal.

w-ng-009.title: Kuli-kuli

instructions.1: Toast the peanuts in a dry frying pan over medium heat, stirring occasionally to avoid burning. Once roasted, remove the skins by rubbing them between your hands or using a cloth to gently press and peel off the skins.
instructions.2: Using a food processor or blender, grind the roasted peanuts to form a peanut butter, working in batches as necessary. This will take around 5-10 minutes depending on power.
instructions.3: Transfer the peanut mixture to a large mixing bowl. Add water, ¼ cup (60 ml) at a time, to the peanut butter, kneading with your hands after each addition. This will swell up the grains in the peanut butter, making it thicker and releasing the oils. Stop adding water once the mixture starts releasing oils. Continue to knead for a further 5 minutes to release as much oil as possible.
instructions.4: Put the mixture into a cheesecloth, and squeeze to release the oils. Transfer the peanut mixture back to the bowl, and set aside the oils for deep-frying.
instructions.5: Stir in the remaining ingredients, mixing well to combine.
instructions.6: Mix in enough water, a tablespoon at a time, until you get a moldable dough, and knead well.
instructions.7: Take teaspoonfuls of the dough and roll them into small balls or form them into flat discs, depending on your preference. You can also shape them into small cylinders or oval shapes, like traditional kuli-kuli. You can experiment with different shapes.
instructions.8: Heat the reserved oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Fry the kuli-kuli pieces in batches, ensuring they don’t overcrowd the pan, until they are golden brown and crispy on all sides (about 4-5 minutes). Be sure to flip them carefully to ensure even frying.
instructions.9: Once fried, remove the kuli-kuli from the oil and place them on a paper towel to drain excess oil. Allow them to cool completely before serving.

w-ng-009.culturalNotes: Kuli-kuli is a traditional Nigerian snack or breakfast dish.

w-ng-010.title: Ofada Rice

instructions.1: Wash the rice thoroughly with water until the rinse water is clear.
instructions.2: Add the rice to a large pot and add enough water to cover the rice by about 2 cm.
instructions.3: Add salt to taste.
instructions.4: Cover the pot and bring the rice to a boil over high heat.
instructions.5: Reduce the heat and let the rice simmer for 20 minutes or until cooked.
instructions.6: Turn off the heat and let the rice rest for 5 minutes before serving.

w-ng-010.culturalNotes: Ofada rice is a local variety of rice in Nigeria, known for its unique flavor and dark brown color.

w-ng-011.title: Ofe Owerri

w-ng-011-i9.name: fresh bell pepper or chile pepper

instructions.1: Clean the meats and dryfish, and cut into pieces.
instructions.2: Add the meats to a pot with seasoning cubes and water and bring to a boil until tender.
instructions.3: Add the dryfish and smoked fish and simmer for 10 minutes.
instructions.4: Stir in the cocoyam paste to thicken the soup, making sure it's well incorporated.
instructions.5: Stir in the palm oil, crayfish, ogiri, and pepper and simmer for 5-10 minutes.
instructions.6: Add okazi leaves and simmer for 3 minutes.
instructions.7: Stir in ugu leaves and simmer for 2-3 minutes.
instructions.8: Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve hot with pounded yam or fufu.

w-ng-011.culturalNotes: Ofe Owerri is a traditional soup from Imo State in Nigeria, typically served with pounded yam or fufu.

w-ng-012.title: Owo Soup

w-ng-012-i3.name: Goat meat or assorted halal meat

instructions.1: Blend the tomatoes and fresh pepper to a paste.
instructions.2: Combine the meat, onion, seasoning cubes, and salt in a pot. Cook for about 3 minutes in its own juices.
instructions.3: Cover the meat with water and simmer until tender.
instructions.4: Add the dried fish, tomato-pepper paste, and ground crayfish to the meat. Add about a cup of water and stir. Let simmer for 10 minutes, stirring to prevent burning.
instructions.5: Dissolve the potash powder in 4 tablespoons of hot water. Strain the mixture carefully and mix the liquid into the soup.
instructions.6: Turn off the heat and allow the soup to cool for about 10 minutes.
instructions.7: Return the soup to the heat and gradually stir in the palm oil.
instructions.8: Remove from the heat and serve with plantains, yam, or any swallow of choice.

w-ng-012.culturalNotes: Owo Soup is a traditional Nigerian dish, typically served with plantains, yam, or any swallow of choice.

w-ng-013.title: Peanut Stew with Beef & Spinach

instructions.1: Cube the beef and brown it in vegetable oil.
instructions.2: Add the onions and garlic and cook for several minutes until the onions start to soften and even color a bit.
instructions.3: Pour in the beef broth and bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until the liquid reduces by half.
instructions.4: Stir in the unsweetened peanut butter until well incorporated.
instructions.5: Add the tomatoes and spinach and cook until the spinach wilts and the peanut butter releases its oils, making the dish shiny.

w-ng-013.culturalNotes: Peanut stew is a popular dish in Nigeria, often served with flatbread like kisra or rice.

w-ng-014.title: Nigerian Ogbono Soup with Pounded Yam

w-ng-014-i1.name: Meat (oxtail, stew beef, tripe, cow skin)

instructions.1: Wash the meat and soak it in water for 30 minutes, then drain it.
instructions.2: Place the meat in a pot and cover it with water. Add the onion and bouillon and bring to a boil over low heat for an hour.
instructions.3: Add the smoked fish, ground crayfish, greens, palm oil, and red pepper flakes. Cook for an additional 30 minutes.
instructions.4: Add the ground egusi and ground ogbono and stir well. Cook for 10 minutes until thickened.
instructions.5: Add salt and pepper to taste. Cook for an additional 5 minutes.
instructions.6: In another pot, place the pounded yam and bring to a boil over low heat for 10 minutes until soft.
instructions.7: Serve the soup with the pounded yam hot.

w-ng-014.culturalNotes: Nigerian Ogbono Soup with Pounded Yam is a traditional dish in Nigeria, known for its rich flavor and creamy texture.

w-gr-001.title: Diples

instructions.1: Mix the flour with water to make a firm dough.
instructions.2: Let the dough rest for 30 minutes.
instructions.3: Cut the dough into small pieces and roll them out thinly.
instructions.4: Fry the pieces in hot oil until golden brown.
instructions.5: Drain the diples on paper towels.
instructions.6: Pour the melted butter and honey over the diples, and add cinnamon.
instructions.7: Serve hot or cold as desired.

w-gr-001.culturalNotes: Diples are a traditional Greek sweet served on special occasions.

w-gr-002.title: Galaktoboureko

instructions.1: Combine sugar, eggs, and semolina in a saucepan. Add milk and vanilla beans. Stir in lemon juice.
instructions.2: Bring the mixture to a boil, stirring constantly with a fork. When it starts boiling, reduce heat and keep stirring for another 10 minutes. Remove the mixture from the heat and let it cool.
instructions.3: Brush each sheet of phyllo dough with melted butter.
instructions.4: Butter a pan and place half the phyllo sheets in it, one by one. Pour the cooled semolina custard over the pastry, and cover with the remaining buttered phyllo.
instructions.5: Sprinkle the pastry with a bit of water.
instructions.6: Bake the pastry in a preheated oven at 180°C for 1 hour. Let it cool before serving.

w-gr-002.culturalNotes: Galaktoboureko is a traditional Greek dessert made from a custard of milk and semolina, wrapped in phyllo dough. It is typically served cold.

w-gr-003.title: Giouvetsi (Traditional Greek Orzo Bake)

instructions.1: Heat olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat; cook meat until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes.
instructions.2: Add pureed tomatoes, garlic, sugar, salt, and pepper. Cover and simmer for 1 hour, stirring occasionally. Set aside.
instructions.3: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
instructions.4: Melt butter in a medium skillet over medium heat and add the orzo. Saute until slightly brown, 3 to 5 minutes.
instructions.5: Transfer orzo to a baking pan, spreading it out evenly. Place the meat on top of the orzo and pour the tomato sauce over the meat. Add hot water.
instructions.6: Cover with aluminum foil and bake in the preheated oven until all water is absorbed and orzo is soft, about 1 hour. If the dish becomes too dry, add more water during baking.

w-gr-003.culturalNotes: Giouvetsi is a traditional Greek dish often served on special occasions. It is usually served with Greek salad.

w-gr-004.title: Air Fryer Beef Kofta Kebabs

instructions.1: Mix the ground beef, onion, parsley, garlic, cumin, coriander, salt, black pepper, and cinnamon in a large bowl until well combined.
instructions.2: Divide the mixture into 8 portions and shape them into oval-shaped patties around the skewers, making sure the point of the skewer is covered.
instructions.3: Place the kebabs on a plate and refrigerate.
instructions.4: Preheat the air fryer to 370 degrees F (188 degrees C).
instructions.5: Stir the yogurt, cucumber, garlic, lemon juice, dill, and kosher salt together in a small bowl and refrigerate until ready to use.
instructions.6: Place 4 skewers in the basket of the air fryer and cook for 10 minutes. Transfer the kebabs to a plate. Repeat with the remaining skewers.
instructions.7: Serve the kebabs with tzatziki sauce.

w-gr-004.culturalNotes: Kofta is a popular dish in many Arab and Middle Eastern countries, often served with tzatziki sauce.

w-gr-005.title: Melomakarono

instructions.1: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
instructions.2: Whisk flour, cinnamon, baking powder, cloves, baking soda, and nutmeg together in a large bowl.
instructions.3: In a separate bowl, beat butter until light and fluffy; add sugar and mix well.
instructions.4: Beat egg yolks and orange juice together in another bowl. Stir egg mixture into the butter mixture gradually while mixing.
